title: Sr Manager, Real Estate and Workplace
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



ALSO is seeking an execution-driven Sr Manager, Real Estate & Workplace, to lead workplace strategy, projects, programs, and teams based in our Palo Alto HQ for a global multi-site portfolio spanning office, R&D labs, commercial hubs, and retail.


This role owns team leadership, strategic planning, critical project execution, and executive-level representation alongside the Director, partnering daily with IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal, Insurance, People, and cross functional key stakeholders. Success requires ability to prioritize in a fast-paced environment, drive R&D projects to execution, disciplined governance, financial rigor, 3rd party management, and the ability to anticipate space and workplace service needs (ie, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial, and moves). Onsite 3-5 days/week, with off-hours availability for time-sensitive and critical issues.



What You Will Do 

Team & Program Leadership

 - Lead the Real Estate & Workplace team (operations, facilities, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial) as deputy lead, balancing competing priorities with long-term focus.

 - Manage projects end to end, including portfolio administration, R&D lab build-outs, workplace programs, and occupancy data.

Strategic Space Planning & Occupancy Analysis

 - Own headcount and occupancy analysis, turning hiring plans and growth into space strategy, capacity models, and scenarios.

 - Drive long-range workplace strategy and partner with Finance and Analytics on forecasting and tradeoff recommendations to leadership.

Vendor, Contract & Budget Management

 - Manage vendors, consultants, landlords, and GCs with negotiation and financial accountability.

 - Own budget tracking, forecasting, and RFPs with Purchasing and Finance, and oversee lease transactions end to end with Legal and Risk.

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Act as the connective tissue across IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal/Compliance, Analytics, and G&A.

 - Support Executive Assistants on space, logistics, and events, and communicate credibly with landlords, brokers, executives, and building inspectors.

Technical R&D Project Delivery & Operations

 - Coordinate lab infrastructure and equipment installs with Engineering and vendors.

 - Partner with the IT and EHS & Security Manager on life-safety and compliance, and serve as a point of contact for after-hours facilities emergencies.

Process Governance & Data Enablement

 - Implement standard PM frameworks, ticketing, and KPI/milestone dashboards.

 - Adopt new technology and AI-assisted tools to streamline workflows as the portfolio grows.



What You Will Bring 

 - 7+ years of progressive real estate, workplace, or facilities operations experience, with demonstrated growth from individual execution into a leadership scope.

 - Track record leading teams and operating as a trusted second-in-command.

 - Comfortable partnering across IT, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and Purchasing, and communicating credibly from AHJs to executives.

 - Working knowledge of commercial leases, vendor contracts, and budget/financial management.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-changing priorities; adaptable to new technology, software, and AI-assisted tools.

 - Familiarity with EHS, physical security concepts, and specialized lab/R&D infrastructure preferred (this role partners with a dedicated EHS & Security Manager rather than owning those programs directly).

 - Experience scaling high-tech, EV, or R&D lab environments strongly preferred.

 - Able to respond to occasional off-hours emergencies.



The salary for this position ranges from $200,000 - $220,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.


Perks and Benefits

 - Robust health coverage. Excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by Also. with FSA & HSA options.

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates.

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny.

 - Flexible time off. 

 - 401(k) match.



Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

Drug Substance Engineering Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Micronization of drug substance is a critical process in API manufacturing for ensuring downstream critical quality attributes. Micronization processes such as pin milling and jet milling leverage feed rate control to optimize the process performance, and while feed rate is well understood for many powder systems there is a gap in understanding the feed rate control of poorly flowing materials in micronization techniques.
The Drug Substance Engineering Intern within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) will help establish a systematic approach to understand how the physical properties of powder systems impact their feeding performance in micronization processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Experimental studies to understand and characterize powder properties
Evaluate performance of micronization techniques (i.e. jet mill, pin mill) with various feed mechanisms
Analyze data and trends to identify signatures for process performance
Develop and verify computational models
Summarize and present findings in departmental and cross-functional settings
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or other related field
Must be enrolled in university for at least one semester following the internship
Preferred Qualifications
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Exposure to comminution processes
Experience with physical characterization techniques (flowability, adhesion, cohesion, bulk density, laser diffraction particle size determination)
Proficient in computational modeling techniques (e.g., fluid dynamics, discrete element method)

Key Responsibilities:
Pricing Strategy and Guidance:
Develop and maintain International pricing guidance for RINVOQ (price corridors and launch and re-pricing recommendations) in line with brand strategy, the Integrated Access Strategy (IAS) and corporate objectives.
Apply the Strategic Pricing Framework to define the price potential of new indications and formulations, and recommend indication and country launch sequencing that maximizes International value.
Develop contracting guidance and access models that address payer objections and affordability concerns while preserving the integrity of RINVOQ's price.
Monitor International pricing policy and competitor pricing, and flag risks and opportunities for RINVOQ early.
Business Cases and Pricing Governance:
Lead the development, review and challenge of RINVOQ pricing business cases from affiliates and Areas, ensuring each is analytically sound, compliant with International pricing governance and ready for decision.
Prepare and present business cases to the Executive Pricing Councils, with a clear recommendation, quantified financial impact, risks and mitigations.
PVTO and IRP Analysis:
Build and run price-volume trade-off (PVTO) analyses to evaluate price and access scenarios, breakeven volumes and the net revenue impact of pricing decisions at market and International level.
Assess International Reference Pricing (IRP) implications of every proposed price change, launch price and confidential agreement. Quantify cross-country spill-over and recommend the sequencing and price levels that preserve the integrity of RINVOQ's price across International markets.
Work with International Pricing analysts to design, run and interpret IRP, PVTO and launch-sequencing models, and turn the outputs into clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Plan and LRP:
Own the RINVOQ pricing assumptions in the annual Plan and Long Range Plan (LRP) process, including price evolution, launch timing, price erosion, IRP impact and risk and opportunity scenarios.
Collect, challenge and align pricing assumptions with Areas, affiliates and Finance, so that forecasts are consistent and explained.
Cross-Functional Partnership:
Area and affiliates (primary partners): help key markets turn International pricing guidance into local outcomes, covering price potential, negotiation strategy, scenarios, fallback positions and objection handling for national and sub-national negotiations.
Therapy Area teams (primary partners): make sure the pricing position is reflected in the RINVOQ IAS and brand strategy, and that indication priorities reflect price potential.

description:

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. This position may be based in Florham Park, NJ, or Mettawa, IL.
The Director, Psychiatry Marketing External Engagement sets the strategy and leads the teams responsible for psychiatry's external expert engagement, Regional Marketing Manager (RMM), and promotional medical education capabilities. This leader ensures that national brand strategy is translated into relevant regional execution, that external expert relationships and engagements generate actionable insights, and that peer-to-peer education addresses healthcare professional needs in a rapidly evolving and highly competitive market. The Director provides enterprise-level leadership across strategy, people, operations, and execution, ensuring that external engagement, regional marketing, and promotional medical education plans are integrated, insight-driven, compliant, and aligned with brand priorities. In close partnership with the broader Marketing team, Medical, Sales Leadership, Field Operations, Compliance, Finance, and agency partners, the Director optimizes investments, strengthens execution, develops leaders and teams, builds scalable capabilities, and serves as a senior strategic thought partner on the brand and across the cross-functional team.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules through Early-Stage Clinical Development.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific and leadership experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
For the Principal Research Scientist I position, we are seeking a highly motivated and experienced data scientist to provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), advanced analytics, and data automation within Analytical R&D. The successful candidate will partner closely with analytical scientists to frame high-value scientific questions, engineer and integrate complex analytical data, and develop fit-for-purpose models, visualizations, and digital solutions that accelerate data-driven decisions across pharmaceutical development.
The candidate will perform and direct data science and application-development activities, mentor and develop scientists, and provide leadership across multiple projects and initiatives. They will conceive, execute, and communicate multidisciplinary strategies; translate between analytical scientists, statisticians, data engineers, software and IT partners; and convert innovative concepts into sustainable, adopted solutions with measurable scientific and business impact.
This role requires a strong combination of data science depth, pharmaceutical or scientific domain awareness, product-oriented solution development, and collaborative leadership. The scientist will help shape the Analytical R&D data science strategy, establish reusable standards and best practices, coordinate initiatives across a global network, and foster productive partnerships with internal data science, statistics, information technology, and R&D organizations.
Responsibilities:
Provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, AI/ML, advanced analytics, visualization, and data automation initiatives supporting pharmaceutical development.
Consult with analytical scientists and project teams to define the scientific or business question, assess data readiness, select appropriate analytical approaches, and translate results into clear recommendations and decisions.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of data products and analytical solutions, including problem framing, data acquisition and integration, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development and validation, visualization, deployment, documentation, user adoption, and lifecycle support.
Develop and apply statistical, machine-learning, chemometric, and/or generative-AI methods to complex analytical data while ensuring approaches are scientifically sound, interpretable, reproducible, and fit for intended use.
Engineer, curate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from laboratory instruments, scientific systems, documents, and development workflows; improve data quality, traceability, accessibility, and reuse.
Design and deliver intuitive applications, dashboards, reports, and automated workflows that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and enable scientists to obtain timely insights from their data.
Mentor, guide, and develop data scientists and scientific colleagues; provide technical coaching, peer review, and hands-on support, and create learning opportunities that strengthen data literacy and analytical capability across the organization.
Lead or coordinate a portfolio of data science initiatives, establish priorities and delivery plans, manage risks and dependencies, and communicate progress, value, and recommendations to project teams and senior stakeholders.
Establish and promote standards for analytical data assessment, model validation, software development, documentation, version control, testing, data governance, and sustainable solution support.
Build and foster a global network with Analytical R&D, Development Sciences, statistics, enterprise data science, IT, and external partners; connect teams to the appropriate expertise and facilitate effective cross-functional execution.
Identify high-value opportunities, generate new scientific proposals, evaluate emerging AI/ML and digital technologies, and champion responsible innovation that advances scientific understanding, development speed, quality, and operational efficiency.
Communicate complex methods and findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences through decision-focused presentations, reports, visualizations, and scientific publications where appropriate.
Ensure solutions and activities comply with applicable safety, quality, regulatory, data-integrity, privacy, security, and AbbVie requirements.
Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Chemometrics, Computational Science, Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related discipline, typically with a minimum of 14 years (BS), 12 years (MS), or 6 years (Ph.D.) of relevant industry experience.
Demonstrated experience applying data science, AI/ML, statistics, or advanced analytics to scientific, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, or other complex R&D problems.
Advanced proficiency in Python and/or R and strong working knowledge of relevant data-science libraries, statistical modeling, machine learning, data visualization, and reproducible analytical workflows.
Experience integrating, cleaning, transforming, and analyzing complex and heterogeneous data; working knowledge of SQL, relational data concepts, APIs, and modern data-management practices.
Demonstrated ability to build and deliver production-quality analytical applications, dashboards, automated workflows, or reusable data products. Experience with tools such as Streamlit, Shiny, cloud platforms, workflow automation, or equivalent technologies is desirable.
Strong understanding of model development and evaluation, experimental design, uncertainty, validation, interpretability, and the limitations and appropriate use of AI/ML methods.
Demonstrated leadership through mentoring, technical direction, project or portfolio leadership, influence across functions, and delivery of complex initiatives. Prior direct people-management experience is beneficial but not required.
Proven ability to partner with domain scientists, quickly learn scientific workflows, translate ambiguous needs into tractable analytical problems, and balance technical rigor with practical, fit-for-purpose delivery.
Experience with software-development practices such as Git/version control, modular coding, testing, documentation, code review, deployment, and lifecycle management.
Excellent analytical problem-solving, project-management, written and oral communication, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain complex concepts to diverse audiences.
Self-motivated, collaborative, and adaptable, with demonstrated scientific curiosity, creativity, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced R&D environment.
Knowledge of pharmaceutical development, CMC, analytical laboratory workflows, regulated environments, data integrity, or scientific data standards is strongly preferred.
Experience with computational chemistry and molecular modeling approaches to investigate molecular properties, structure–property relationships, or other scientific questions relevant to pharmaceutical development is desirable.

description:
About AbbVie

AbbVie’s Biologics CMC organization develops processes to support the advancement and manufacture of biologic medicines. AbbVie is seeking a highly motivated scientist to lead development of microbial-based recombinant peptide production processes. This position will serve as a technical lead across expression-system and strain development, fermentation, recovery, purification, and scale-up.
Recombinant production of short peptides can be challenging due to intracellular degradation, low expression, aggregation, and limited solubility. The successful candidate will develop and optimize practical strategies to address these challenges and advance robust, scalable processes for therapeutic peptide production. When aligned with program needs, the candidate will also evaluate and apply genetic code expansion (GCE) strategies to enable the site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids. The role will collaborate with cross-functional partners and contribute to process development, technology evaluation, and technology transfer activities.
Responsibilities:
Lead recombinant peptide process-development activities, including expression strategy, host and clone screening, process optimization, and scale-up.
Design and evaluate expression constructs and microbial hosts, including  Escherichia coli  and yeast, for peptide production.
Develop and assess fusion-tag and carrier-protein strategies—including His-tag, GST, SUMO, and inclusion-body expression—to improve peptide stability, expression, host tolerance, and recovery.
Design and conduct clone-screening studies using microscale cultivation, parallel bioreactors, and other appropriate scale-down or high-throughput approaches.
Develop and optimize peptide recovery processes, including cell harvest and lysis, inclusion-body isolation and processing, and chemical or enzymatic cleavage of fusion partners.
Troubleshoot peptide-specific process challenges, such as aggregation, low solubility, degradation, incomplete cleavage, and co-eluting impurities; recommend and pursue appropriate solutions.
Interpret analytical results, including HPLC, UPLC, and LC-MS data, to assess peptide identity, mass accuracy, purity, and process-related impurities; partner with analytical teams to address characterization needs.
Evaluate emerging technologies and process approaches for recombinant peptide production, including genetic code expansion when relevant to program needs.
Apply AI/ML approaches, where appropriate, to analyze peptide sequence, structure, and experimental data in support of design, optimization, and candidate prioritization.
Communicate scientific plans, progress, challenges, conclusions, and recommendations clearly to project teams and other stakeholders.
Mentor junior scientists and provide technical direction in recombinant peptide bioprocessing.
Contribute to scientific publications and presentations at conferences, as appropriate.
Maintain a high level of productivity while managing priorities and timelines; follow applicable corporate standards for safety, quality, and compliance.
PhD with typically 4+ years of relevant experience, master’s degree or equivalent education with 10+  years of relevant experience or Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education with typically 12+ years of relevant experience is required.
Thorough theoretical and practical understanding of relevant scientific disciplines, with hands-on experience in microbial physiology and recombinant expression systems, particularly  E. coli  and/or yeast.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to address scientific or development questions.
Experience developing or optimizing expression processes for peptides, small proteins, or other products susceptible to degradation, or instability.
Experience with strain or clone screening, fermentation, and process optimization; familiarity with bioreactors and scale-down or parallel cultivation approaches.
Demonstrated experience with preparative chromatography and peptide or protein purification, as well as peptide recovery and fusion-partner cleavage strategies.
Strong experimental design, data interpretation, troubleshooting, scientific writing, and oral communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and timelines and work effectively in a matrixed, cross-functional environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience developing or manufacturing complex therapeutic peptides, particularly GLP-1 or related incretin peptides, in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company or start-up environment.
Experience applying genetic code expansion to incorporate non-canonical amino acids at defined positions using engineered orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs and codon reassignment.

•Drive the site capital long range plan from development to submission.

description:
The Opportunity
Typography is central to how ideas are communicated. If you're passionate about beautifully created design, have deep curiosity about what AI can do, and take personal responsibility for creating products that people love; then this may be the role for you. Adobe Fonts supports millions of creatives in choosing and using typefaces across fonts.adobe.com, Express, Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat, and more Creative Cloud platforms. Our Internal Services team provides the platform engineering and deployment backbone for all of these. We manage CI/CD, deployment approaches, the services and data layers our engineers depend on, our observability and security stance, and increasingly the agentic tools that transform how our entire organization delivers software.
We're seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer to lead this exciting journey in our San Francisco location.
What you'll do
Own and evolve our deployment platform. Lead strategy for CI/CD, PR environments, and release safety across a mixed fleet that includes containerized services, serverless services, and static front ends.
Build the foundation for AI-accelerated development. Help build our agent factory and grow our internal agentic toolkit and skill library.
Ship inference applications at scale. Take greenfield services from spec to production and standardize our ML/inference footprint.
Modernize our services for the AI era. Identify where an existing service is held back by its current build and lead the fix.
Rethink our security posture for agentic threats. Lead how we secure autonomous agents and their tool use.
Expose Adobe Fonts to the agentic ecosystem. Extend our Model Context Protocol (MCP) surface and conversational, intent-based font discovery.
Work higher up the stack, too. Contribute directly to search, browse, discovery, and the customer-facing experiences our platform powers.
Hold ownership over what you deliver to production, encompassing on-call support, incident management, and the reliability of the services and pipelines that the entire organization depends upon.
Set technical direction and multiply the team. Write the development docs, run the technical reviews, and mentor engineers.

Software engineering
Deep full-stack fundamentals and craft — build, testing, code quality, code review — plus system development and production maturity: latency, scale, reliability, observability, and on-call ownership.
Ships and owns services end to end, and reasons fluently across the whole stack: front end (JavaScript/TypeScript, React or Web Components), application services (Ruby/Rails, Python, Go, and comfort picking up others), and the SRE/config/hardware layer beneath (Terraform, Chef, Kubernetes/Helm, AWS).

Strong CI/CD ownership (Jenkins or equivalent), containerization and orchestration, infrastructure-as-code, and AWS (EC2/ASG, IAM, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront). Experience making deployment fast, safe, and self-service — ephemeral/preview environments, progressive delivery, rollback strategy.
Solid grasp of the data and messaging layers behind real services, including relational, caching, search, and event-driven/pub-sub. You know how to run migrations and upgrades without downtime.
AI/agentic proficiency
Hands-on understanding of building AI-enabled systems: agent runtimes, tool calling, MCP, LLM/inference serving, and the infrastructure around them — evaluation, feedback loops, observability, and sandboxed execution.
A security outlook for this new surface — you think about how agentic systems fail and get abused, and proactively build guardrails accordingly.
Leadership & scope
Track record of delivering high-impact platform work used across multiple teams, leading complex cross-team technical efforts, and balancing near-term delivery with long-term maintainability, security, and operability.
Excellent written and verbal communication.
Typically 12+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated senior-level impact.

Ruby on Rails at scale, and experience decomposing or modernizing a large monolith.
GPU/model-serving infrastructure and low-latency inference (e.g. SageMaker, Kubernetes GPU platforms); search-engine internals (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, vector/hybrid search).
Experience building developer platforms, internal tooling, or agent harnesses adopted by other teams.
Event-driven architectures and secrets-management platforms (Vault, CyberArk).

description:

Calendar and Scheduling
• Own calendars for leaders spanning Americas, EMEA, and APJ, resolving conflicts and making trade-offs among time, quality, and resources based on business need
• Coordinate multi-country travel, including itineraries, visas, and expense reconciliation across regions
Team Operations

title: Learning & Development Program Manager, AWS Controls Engineering
description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global Data Centers infrastructure. We support all AWS data centers power, and cooling equipment related monitoring and automatic controls system that ensure our customers have continual access to the AWS cloud services.
You’ll join a diverse team of industrial controls, and systems engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
As part of the AMER controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for defining the onboarding, training, and career development of Engineers, Technicians, and Program Managers on the AMER Controls Deployment, Service and Fleet (CDS) fleet. You combine instructional design expertise with a working understanding of industrial controls systems (BMS/EPMS), data center operations, or mission-critical engineering environments. You will be responsible for architecting a single standardized training program from the ground up, redesign the existing onboarding experience and accelerate new hire effectiveness.
This role demands excellent verbal and written communication skills, strong program management discipline, and the ability to partner across engineering, operations, and leadership stakeholders throughout AMER.
Key job responsibilities
As a CDS L&D manager, you will
Design, build, and continuously improve a standardized Controls training program covering the full onboarding lifecycle for Controls Engineers and Controls Technicians, including a structured 90-day experience with weekly shadowing plans, monthly partner team rotations, and qualification milestones.
Develop and deliver technical curricula aligned to the daily work of Controls roles — BMS and EPMS system architecture, sequence of operations, controls logic programming, industrial protocols (BACnet, MODBUS, MQTT), commissioning, root cause analysis, and alarm management.
Build role-specific training tracks: Technician content covering field device installation, calibration, provisioning, electrical schematics, and red-line documentation; Engineer content covering project scoping, budgeting, vendor management, and service contract financial oversight.
Create and maintain skill assessments that measure readiness by role and level; track qualification pass rates, manager-assessed proficiency ratings, and onboarding satisfaction as program effectiveness signals.
Partner with Controls Engineers, Technicians, team managers, and DC Operations stakeholders across AMER to align curriculum to operational needs, coordinate SME content reviews, and prevent training materials from going stale.
Own the training program roadmap, milestones, and dependencies — including the onboarding platform, shadowing tooling, and training lab and communicate program status and metrics to senior leadership through regular reporting cadences.
Explore and partner with education institutions and trade schools to influence and tailor their curriculum to support campus hiring for AWS CDS team and develop in-house training program to get the new hires trained.
About the team
This role directly support following three Controls job families. Understanding their day-to-day work is essential to building training that is practical, relevant, and immediately applicable.
Controls Engineers
Controls Engineers troubleshoot and perform Root Cause Analysis on Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) issues; manage the full project lifecycle from scoping and budgeting through commissioning; develop and modify controls logic and GUIs; financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts; and participate in AWS global on-call schedules. They work with cross-functional stakeholders across construction, operations, and vendor management, and frequently travel to in-operation data centers.
Controls Technicians
Controls Technicians deploy, service, and upgrade BMS and EPMS across multiple data centers. They perform point-to-point checkouts, first-line diagnostics, server and controller provisioning, sensor installation and calibration, commissioning support, change management documentation, and factory witnessed tests. They also mentor Facilities team members and actively manage service agreements.
Systems Engineers
Systems Engineers are responsible for Deploy, manage, and support large-scale Windows and Linux environments, including virtualization platforms and networking components. They also create and maintain automation solutions using PowerShell, Python, or Bash, focusing on scalable deployment processes and infrastructure management

- 5+ years of with Learning & Development and course facilitation experience
- Experience developing or delivering training programs across multiple sites or regions
- 7+ years of program or project management experience
- 4+ years of owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience

title: Sr. Product Manager – Technical, Leo Futures, Leo Connectivity
description:
Amazon Leo is building a constellation of 3,000+ Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband connectivity to customers around the world. The Leo Connectivity Product team is responsible for defining and delivering the end-to-end networking and service experiences that connect customers — consumers, enterprises, and the public sector — to the Leo network.
We are seeking a highly technical Sr. Product Manager to own product definition for future generations of Leo’s satellite connectivity system. This is a strategic, cross-functional role focused on identifying the customer problems we will solve with next-generation architectures. You will work at the intersection of vehicle engineering, software engineering, modeling and simulation, and the PMT teams building our first-generation network, constellation and customer devices — synthesizing insights across all of them to define what comes next.
This role requires someone who thrives in ambiguity. The problems are not yet well-defined, the solution space is wide open, and the timelines may be long. You will frame ill-defined challenges into actionable product strategies, drive system-level trade studies with modeling and simulation teams and translate technical possibilities into customer-centric product direction. This is a high-visibility individual contributor role based in Redmond, WA.
*** Export Control Requirement***
- Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Key job responsibilities
- Define the product vision and requirements for future-generation satellite connectivity systems, grounded in deep understanding of customer problems across consumer, enterprise, and public sector segments.
- Drive system-level trade studies in partnership with modeling and simulation teams — translating simulation outputs into product requirements and investment recommendations.
- Partner deeply with vehicle engineering and software engineering to understand technical constraints and opportunities that inform future system architectures.
- Collaborate with PMTs owning first-generation constellation systems and customer antenna products to identify gaps, lessons learned, and opportunities that shape future generations.
- Frame ambiguous, long-horizon problems into structured product strategies with clear hypotheses, evaluation criteria, and decision frameworks.
- Write PRFAQs, technical narratives, and investment proposals that articulate the customer need, technical approach, and business case for future system capabilities.
- Represent the futures roadmap in leadership reviews, clearly communicating trade-offs, dependencies, and strategic rationale to senior technical and business stakeholders.
A day in the life
Your morning might begin with a review of simulation results from the modeling team — a new trade study has landed overnight comparing architectural approaches for a capability that could unlock performance improvements for enterprise customers. You dig into the data, identify the assumptions that need stress-testing, and draft follow-up questions for the simulation engineers.
Mid-morning, you’re in a working session with vehicle engineering, walking through how a proposed design change to the satellite bus impacts the connectivity services you’re defining. You push on the customer experience implications and propose a set of requirements that preserve flexibility for future service evolution.
After lunch, you sit down with a PMT colleague who owns our payload software. Together you review field data and customer feedback, looking for patterns that signal where the current architecture falls short and where the next generation needs to leap forward. You capture three hypotheses to validate with simulation runs.
The afternoon is heads-down writing time. You’re drafting a narrative that frames a customer problem — one that doesn’t have an obvious solution yet — and propose an evaluation framework for the engineering team to assess multiple architectural paths. You end the day in a cross-functional sync, aligning vehicle, software, and simulation teams on priorities for the next sprint of trade studies.
About the team
You’ll be part of the Leo Connectivity Product team — a group of product and technology leaders responsible for defining the end-to-end connectivity experience for Leo’s customers. Our team spans device products, networking services, enterprise solutions, and future systems.
We value deep technical curiosity, comfort with ambiguity, and a relentless focus on the customer problems worth solving. We operate with a builder’s mentality — moving fast on the things we understand and moving deliberately on the things that require getting it right. We are a team that debates rigorously, decides clearly, and supports each other once a direction is set.
We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We believe the best products come from teams with varied perspectives and experiences.

- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning
- Working knowledge of RF systems, propagation physics, spectrum allocation, and the physical-layer constraints that govern satellite connectivity performance.
- 5+ years of experience in aerospace, satellite communications, or telecommunications systems.
Preferred qualifications: - Background in satellite communications, space systems, or LEO constellation architectures.
- Experience defining products that span multiple customer segments (consumer, enterprise, public sector).
- Experience working with large-scale simulation and modeling systems to inform product decisions and system architecture trade-offs.

- Proven ability to influence without authority across multiple engineering disciplines (hardware, software, systems).
- Experience with Amazon’s product development mechanisms (PRFAQs, narratives, working backwards).

title: Cellular RF System Architect
description:

title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer - Platforms Engineering, Enterprise Technology Services
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. Most software engineering roles hand off testing to one team and operations to another. Here you own all of it. As a Software Engineer on Forge, you'll design, build, test, ship, and run the platform Apple's engineering teams build on, working closely with those teams to find where the infrastructure beneath them gets in the way and fixing it.
Forge is part of Enterprise Technology Services (ETS), within Apple's Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization, the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. Forge is building the platform Apple's engineering organizations can use to take a service from code to running in production. That path has traditionally run through a series of separate specialist systems. We are bringing it together on a common platform with a shared core, so a team goes from allocated capacity to a live production service without assembling the pieces themselves. Our job is to get teams to production quickly, on a platform that stays secure and reliable without them having to think about it.
Our charter is deliberately wide and still growing, reaching from the physical fleet in the data center to the surfaces engineering teams build against, and extending into new environments and new classes of infrastructure as Apple's needs evolve. We are a small team with outsized reach, bringing an AI-first mindset to how the platform operates and improves itself, and the best work we do takes one team's hardest problem and turns it into a capability every team inherits.
As a Forward Deployed Software Engineer, you will embed with the engineering teams who use our platforms, then build the software that solves their problems. This is a software engineering-first role that goes well beyond feature development: you will sit with a customer team to understand their applications and workflows, translate ambiguous requirements into a technical design, write the production code, integrate it with existing systems, and stay with it through deployment and operational readiness. We run what we build, so you will also share an on-call rotation for the services the team owns — which is the fastest way to learn where the platform still falls short.
The work spans Go backend services, React and TypeScript applications, REST and gRPC APIs, distributed systems, and automation that reaches into public cloud, private cloud, Kubernetes, virtual machines, and bare-metal environments. You will also build AI-assisted capabilities — LLM integrations, and agentic workflows — along with the evaluations and quality controls that make those capabilities measurable and trustworthy enough to run in production.
You will move comfortably from a technical discussion with an engineering customer to designing a solution, writing the code, and validating that it works reliably at scale. You will approach loosely defined problems with curiosity and sound judgement, and you will know when a recurring customer request should become a reusable platform capability rather than another one-off integration. You care about clean, maintainable code, thoughtful architecture, and operational reliability, and you are as motivated by simplifying an existing system as by building a new one.
In a team with daring goals and real autonomy, you will take utmost ownership of what you ship — and measure your success by the engineering problems you solve and the lasting improvements you leave behind in the platforms other teams build on.

Operating at the intersection of Core Animation, SwiftUI, and RealityKit, you'll advance the architecture that renders windows, text, and controls as spatial content in real time. You'll also shape RealityView, the API through which developers combine app UI with 3D content. Your work will define the visual quality and performance characteristics of spatial UI, establishing the foundation on which developers and users interact with apps across Apple's vision ecosystem.
Description
As a Spatial UI Rendering Engineer on the RealityKit team, you'll own the rendering quality, power, and performance of spatial UI and RealityView. You'll drive the evolution of the rendering pipeline that brings Core Animation content into RealityKit, and develop the GPU techniques necessary to ensure UI elements maintain exceptional clarity and performance under spatial viewing conditions. You'll also own how RealityView renders app UI and 3D content together, from the underlying rendering integration to the developer-facing behavior and APIs. You'll address complex rendering challenges, including maintaining legibility as viewing distance and render resolution change, rendering UI and 3D content together seamlessly, managing large texture workloads efficiently, and sustaining stable frame rates, memory, and power across extended sessions. You'll collaborate closely with the Core Animation, UI frameworks (UIKit, AppKit, and SwiftUI), Metal, and GPU teams to deliver cohesive solutions that meet Apple's standards for performance and user experience.

Base is scaling the future of energy, and we’re looking for a Journeyman Electrician who thrives in the field. You will be on-site daily—pulling wire, opening panels, troubleshooting real problems, and setting the standard through action. You are the technical backbone of our Austin, TX battery fleet.  - Emergent Support: Participate in a scheduled on-call rotation to address urgent night/weekend electrical issues.

On every deal, you work with the teams who will use the building to scope what they actually need, then source the options, underwrite them, and negotiate the deal through a certificate of occupancy.  - Scope new sites with the teams who will use it before we tour anything: footprint, power, dock doors, clear height, battery storage and fire code requirements, parking, and timing

 - Build the underwriting on every deal we look at: base rent, opex, tenant improvements, escalations, abatement, parking, and yield on cost, with side-by-side scenario analysis so we know what we are trading away

 - On larger projects, build the lease versus own, build-to-suit, and yield-on-cost comparisons so leadership can weigh the options side by side

 - Redline and negotiate LOIs, leases, and amendments alongside our brokers and in-house counsel

 - Get ahead of expansion in existing markets by flagging which facilities are running out of room before it becomes an operations problem

 - Right-size the network: partner with deployments to produce utilization metrics for every distribution facility, then downsize or exit the ones that are not earning their footprint

 - Build the internal motion for real estate sourcing so deployments, launch, operations, and finance all plug into one process instead of five side conversations

 - Maintain the system of record for the portfolio: commencement dates, renewal windows, ROFO and ROFR rights, certificates of occupancy, insurance, and landlord contacts

 - Write the playbook as you go, so each new launch runs faster than the last and can be handed to the team running that market

 - You build the process without being asked. You have taken a messy, manual workflow and turned it into something other people rely on

Lead complex economic damages and financial analyses in commercial disputes, including lost profits, breach of contract, intellectual property, business interruption, shareholder and other business disputes.

Use quantitative analysis and data analytics to support damages calculations, forensic investigations, post-acquisition disputes, and other litigation-related inquiries.

Conduct engagements in compliance with applicable professional, legal, regulatory, and firm requirements.
Manage a broad spectrum of matters involving investigations, litigation support, post-acquisition disputes, and insurance claims.
Lead a broad spectrum of matters involving economic damages, litigation support, forensic accounting investigations, post-acquisition disputes, and other complex financial disputes.
Position the team for successful engagement execution, quality results, and client satisfaction by clearly working within project parameters, managing resources and processes, and anticipating/resolving issues.
Serve as a senior advisor to clients and counsel, translating complex financial and accounting issues into clear, defensible analyses and practical litigation strategies.
Lead engagement execution, including scope, workplan, staffing, budgets, quality, risk management, expert-report development, and client satisfaction.
Manage engagement setup and completion activities, including conflicts, engagement letters, billing, collections, and other engagement administration.
Develop and maintain trusted relationships with outside counsel, in-house legal teams, executives, and other senior client stakeholders.
Recruit, mentor, and develop professionals across the damages and broader Disputes & Investigations team, including development of future expert witnesses.

Originate and expand economic damages and litigation support engagements through an established network of law firms, corporate clients, and referral relationships.
Build Crowe’s market position in economic damages and litigation support, with an expectation of developing into or continuing as a recognized testifying expert.

Collaborate with Crowe partners and leaders across Advisory to identify disputes, litigation, and expert-services opportunities within existing client relationships.
Maintain and expand an external network of attorneys, experts, corporate decision-makers, and industry contacts to generate opportunities and strengthen Crowe’s brand in the disputes market.
Represent Crowe through relevant legal, accounting, damages, and industry organizations, conferences, CLE/CPE programs, publications, and other thought-leadership activities.
Develop a recognized area of expertise within economic damages and litigation support and contribute to Crowe industry and market initiatives.

Draft, review, and support expert reports, rebuttal reports, declarations, presentations, and trial demonstratives that clearly communicate complex damages and financial analyses.
Present complex financial concepts and conclusions to attorneys, executives, boards, arbitrators, judges, and juries in a clear and credible manner.

Deep knowledge of economic damages methodologies and financial analysis, with experience in areas such as lost profits, breach of contract, intellectual property, business valuation, business interruption, shareholder disputes, or other complex commercial litigation.

Demonstrated business development success, including an established network of attorneys and/or corporate relationships, a track record of originating or expanding engagements, and the ability to build a sustainable book of business at Crowe.
Strong leadership and people-management experience, including supervising, mentoring, developing, and evaluating professionals and building teams capable of supporting complex expert matters.

title: Manager, New Verticals - Pharmacy Strategy & Operations
location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA
description:
About the Team
The New Verticals team is building the future of local commerce through expanding our product offerings on our marketplace platform. We launched in 2020 and have since then built world-class operations to delight our customers with access to Grocery, Convenience, Alcohol, Pharmacy and Retail delivery through our marketplace. We focus on building new businesses and scale them - this team is focused on building our Pharmacy business from the ground up.
About the Role
As a Manager on the Pharmacy Strategy & Operations team, you will own the growth and merchant engine for DoorDash's Pharma business. You will build and execute the go-to-market plan that brings pharmacy merchants onto DoorDash, grows their volume, and keeps them. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Partnerships, Marketing, Finance, Legal, and New Verticals platform teams to be successful.
You'll be responsible for turning the pharmacy opportunity into a repeatable motion: planning and launching GTM programs, pitching and negotiating with merchants, and shaping how we speak to returning customers about pharmacy on DoorDash. You are the owner for knowing how Pharma merchants are performing, where the funnel leaks, and where to place the next bet to drive growth. You turn targets into operating plans, and plans into measurable outcomes.
This role requires strong commercial instincts and comfort with data. You should move fluently between merchant-level detail and business-level economics, build frameworks for tradeoffs and prioritization, and familiarity with modeling different scenarios and outcomes. Experience using SQL and data visualization tools is a plus.
You will report into the GM of Pharmacy S&O and be an individual contributor, with the opportunity to build a team in the future.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Strategize. From first principles, you’ll develop the optimal strategy for best serving all sides of the marketplace - dashers, merchants and consumers.
Operate. Own tracking dashboards and manage week over week metrics to drive high quality operations.
Analyze. Build models using Excel and SQL to evaluate the economic, operational and strategic costs and benefits of various programs and experiments — and increasingly, use AI to accelerate and deepen that analysis.
Experiment. You’ll transform strategies into operational experiments, product features and net-new tooling that create measurable outcomes.
Build with AI. You'll use AI tools to automate manual processes, build new prototypes and develop product visions. You'll be expected to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI in your day-to-day work, and share what you learn with the team.
Lead, collaborate and Influence. You’ll partner with and influence cross-functional teams including growth, quality, finance, product and engineering to launch initiatives to the finish line.
We’re excited about you because…
You have 6-8+ years of experience. You've succeeded in similar cultures that are highly analytical and cross-functional (whether in tech, e-commerce, operations, strategy, consulting, banking, or a related experience). Merchant-facing or healthcare/pharmacy experience is a plus.
You are an owner. You're always looking for opportunities to better your work product and own the outcome – both the good and the bad.
You're entrepreneurial. You have a bias for action and are able to build things from the ground up.
You're analytical. You let data win arguments, and you're comfortable pulling your own data in SQL, building models, and building the tools you need to create 10x outcomes.
You are AI Native. You root cause problems with a systems first approach and can identify how to automate repeatable tasks using AI tools like Claude, Cursor, Gemini or Copilot.
You're equally comfortable operating at 10,000 feet and 1 foot. You don't hesitate to get in the weeds and operate at the lowest level of detail, but you're just as comfortable thinking long-term and inspiring a team.
You're a persuasive communicator. You can pitch and negotiate with senior merchant stakeholders and align internal partners around a plan.

description:
About Flexport:
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Build the operational and technical skill set that runs global trade
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. We're shaping the future of a $10T industry with technology and people who understand it end to end. The Rotational Development Program (RDP) exists because that combination — real supply chain fluency plus the ability to build and automate — doesn't exist at scale in the market today. So we're building it ourselves.
This is an 18-month program, not a rotation for rotation's sake. Every assignment is live, revenue-generating work. Every participant leaves with a certification in AI and low-code tooling running alongside their operational and commercial training. And every graduate places into a role with real scope: primarily Account Management, with paths into Automation Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering/Consulting, Sales Engineering, or a traditional Ops/Sales/Customs track.
What you'll do
You'll rotate through three functions, six months each, with AI/low-code curriculum running continuously across all three:
Gateway Ops (Air or Ocean). Own the shipment lifecycle. Execute bookings, manage exceptions, and hold data integrity to Flexport's standard. Build your first automation and reporting skills through structured coursework running in parallel.
Customs. Become a global trade expert by navigating the complex world of customs regulations to ensure goods comply with international laws. Simultaneously, move into applied technical work: SQL, workflow automation, Lean process improvement, etc.
Sales / Account Management. Take on go-to-market work and build client-facing skills, operating with more independence. Your capstone: identify a real business problem in the function you're sitting in and build the tooling or process fix that solves it. You'll present it to leadership at graduation.
Throughout the program, you'll get:
A day-to-day manager in your current rotation and a Rotation Program Manager tracking your development, with mid-point and end-of-rotation evaluations at every stage.
Certifications in AI/low-code tooling, from foundational bootcamp through applied builds to a capstone project.
Bi-weekly cohort touchpoints and a standing alumni mentor community.
Increased earning potential as you clear program benchmarks
This role is for you if you
Are on track to graduate, or recently graduated, and want to build a career at the intersection of supply chain operations and technology — not just run one or the other.
Are genuinely curious about AI and low-code tooling and want to build real fluency, not just check a resume box.
Can operate with minimal supervision, prioritize a high volume of work, and communicate clearly under pressure.
Want real ownership fast? This program hands you live client and business work from the very beginning — it is not a shadowing or classroom based program.
Have a "compliance-first" mindset. We operate in a heavily regulated industry, and that matters in every rotation.
Ready to build the future of global trade — and the skill set to run it?
Apply now.

We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

This role will report to the cathode process development team and support multiple next-generation process development to make and assemble our gas diffusion electrode cathode. You will participate in benchtop and pilot production trials and work to develop and improve novel electrode manufacturing techniques. You’ll use your manufacturing expertise to work closely with material scientists, equipment design engineers, operations, and facilities teams to design, develop, scale, and control revolutionary gas diffusion cathode manufacturing processes for Form Energy’s Iron-Air multi-day battery.

This role provides an exciting opportunity to make a significant and daily impact on a cutting-edge battery technology that will revolutionize the electric grid and bring major improvements to grid reliability and sustainability.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Fine-tune and optimize new equipment with a focus on safety and process capability

 - Conduct engineering trials and data collection with careful attention to detail and effective documentation

 - Document and improve the process steps required to deliver high-quality prototypes of product-scale cathodes to be used in Form Energy’s batteries by authoring SOPs using Microsoft Word or equivalent software.

 - Facilitate the transfer of knowledge and new processes from the Process Development Team to the Manufacturing Engineering Team through in-depth training and on-the-floor operations support

 - Troubleshoot mechanical problems that occur during the commissioning of new prototype equipment

 - Problem-solve and troubleshoot novel mechanical challenges on first-of-its-kind pilot equipment and manufacturing processes

 - Build and test prototype manufacturing equipment

 - Be a champion for safety in the development of new equipment and manufacturing processes




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 5+ years of experience as a technician or in a hands-on role in a fast-paced manufacturing environment with demonstrated manufacturing process knowledge

 - Experience executing manufacturing or engineering trials with diligent attention to detail and a high standard for quality

 - Hands-on experience with manufacturing equipment and desire to roll up your sleeves and fill the gaps where necessary

 - Well-developed written and verbal communication skills with a positive get-it-done attitude

 - Moderate level of comfort with computer software such as Microsoft Excel, Word, and Powerpoint
   
   


WHERE YOU'LL WORK:

This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. 



 #LI-Onsite



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed. 



To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.




If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.

Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will never solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.

POSITION LOCATION:  Remote in the United States
Compensation includes a  lower base , but total earnings with commissions typically fall  between $90K–$120K , with  senior‑level associates landing toward the top end . About the Role:
As an Inside Sales Representative for our SpringWell water filtration business, you'll help guide homeowners to the right high-performance filtration and treatment solutions. You'll manage a high volume of inbound leads by phone, chat and email, using consultative selling to recommend tailored, trustworthy solutions.
Success in this role comes from learning quickly, taking initiative, communicating clearly, and partnering across teams to refine processes and elevate the customer experience. You'll build trust with homeowners by asking the right questions, simplifying complex product information, and recommending solutions that best meet their needs and goals.
Key Responsibilities:
Be the first voice homeowners hear from SpringWell, engaging inbound prospects by phone, chat, email and scheduled follow-ups, and independently owning the full sales cycle for standard and moderately complex system configurations.
Conduct structured, needs-based discovery to understand each customer's water quality concerns, translating test results and technical detail into plain language a homeowner can act on.
Educate customers on SpringWell products and solutions in a clear, consultative way, and recommend system configurations aligned to their needs, budget and installation requirements.
Progress assigned opportunities through defined sales stages toward close, confidently handling common objections on pricing, installation and product differentiation.
Deliver a professional, trust-building customer experience that drives conversion and builds long-term brand credibility - the kind of conversation that makes someone recommend us to a neighbor.
Maintain accurate, timely CRM records including call notes, follow-ups and pipeline activity, so the forecast reflects reality.
Keep building product depth across system capabilities, installation factors and competitive alternatives, escalating advanced technical scenarios while learning to resolve them independently over time.
Meet or exceed assigned revenue and productivity targets, balancing high inbound lead volume with conversion quality and follow-up discipline, and spotting upsell or cross-sell opportunities within approved product configurations.
Share what you're hearing (recurring questions, objections and water concerns) with teammates, marketing and product, so the whole team gets sharper.
2+ years of inside sales experience, with a track record of results
Proven ability to independently manage a full sales cycle from qualification through close
Strong needs-based discovery and objection-handling skills
Experience selling higher-consideration or consultative products, rather than purely transactional ones
The ability to manage high inbound lead volume while maintaining conversion discipline
Proficiency with CRM systems for managing pipeline, follow-ups and forecasting
Preferred Qualifications:
Background selling water treatment, home services, or other technical home-improvement systems (e.g., HVAC or solar).
Deep understanding of residential water quality concerns and installation requirements.

In addition to base salary, employees will participate in either an annual bonus plan based on company and individual performance, or a role-based sales incentive plan.

description:
Fortune Brands Innovations (NYSE: FBIN) is an industry-leading home, security and digital products company with a portfolio of trusted brands, including Moen, House of Rohl, Therma-Tru, Larson, Master Lock, Yale residential, and Sentry Safe.

Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Manager, Product Integrity to join our Connected Products team .  Product Integrity is the team that confirms our connected products — Flo by Moen water devices, Yale and August smart locks, and Master Lock connected padlocks — do what their requirements say they do before they reach a customer. This role leads that team and owns the bridge between requirements and proof: taking what Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance ask for and turning it into tests with a method, a sample size, and a pass/fail criterion.
The role also owns 100% end-of-line testing at the factory, including test fixture design and test software. Depending on test complexity, fixtures are built fully in-house or developed with a supplier.
We are looking for a leader who can spearhead the product quality and integrity function covering test definition, systems integration, test execution, and holding a high product integrity bar. This leader will lead a hardware testing team.  The right person understands the whole product — electrical, mechanical, firmware, and how they interact — well enough to argue a requirement with Product, an interface with Architecture, and the statistics with Reliability, and then run the lab that proves it.
Position location: this position is eligible to work in a hybrid environment out of our North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA locations.
What you will own
The Product Integrity team. Lead a team of test engineers covering production and 100% test, hardware test, reliability test, quality inspection, and overall confirmation of product requirements. You set the direction and the standard; the team executes.
Requirements into tests. Turn every hardware requirement in the PRD — from Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance — into a testable requirement with a method, a sample size, an acceptance criterion, and a gate. Product defines the design envelope; you define how we test to it.
Gate evidence. Every stage gate (EVT, DVT, PVT) carries your evidence package: what was tested, against which requirement, with what result.
Reliability. Define the reliability test plan for each program and own the statistics behind it: sample sizes, confidence levels, and acceleration factors for environmental testing.
Production test. Develop fixtures and test software that meet approved cycle times, with test limits tied to expected field performance.
Field performance. Review returns and field data, and feed what you learn back into requirements and test plans.
The team and the logistics
Team: test engineers covering production test, hardware test, reliability test, and quality inspection. The lab is in North Olmsted.
Location: North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA. If based in San Francisco, expect occasional travel to North Olmsted.
Travel: ~15%. Travel to factories in Nogales and Tecate, Mexico; Hanoi, Vietnam; and between North Olmsted and San Francisco.
Qualifications
10+ years on connected consumer hardware spanning electrical, mechanical, and firmware.
Experience developing factory test fixtures at both board level and end of line.
Experience writing requirements and V&V plans.
Reliability engineering fluency: accelerated life testing, Weibull and AFR math, sample sizing at a stated confidence, HALT/HASS, thermal, drop, and cycle life. You can design a plan and read a failure.
Production test experience: fixtures, test software, DFT, cycle time, and yield at a contract manufacturer.
Has led a small technical team and is comfortable setting direction for test engineers who are more hands-on than you.
Nice to have
Battery power model development.
Sensor products with calibration and drift requirements.
Sealed or outdoor enclosures.
RF performance characterization.
Certification literacy across safety (UL), RF (FCC), and interop (Matter/CSA); NSF/IAPMO for water products or BHMA for locks.

Miller is building a new software-as-a-service business from the ground up: cloud software for the welding and fabrication industry, backed by nearly a century of industry leadership and the resources of ITW. Own delivery of projects end to end
Take high-level, often ambiguous problems, break them into well-defined work, and deliver independently.

Deliver software enhancements
Reviewing code from external development partners
Improve software development, testing, and deployment processes.

Hands-on experience building and operating cloud-hosted web applications or services in production (Azure preferred).

Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and monitoring production systems.
Demonstrated ability to own delivery end to end, work through ambiguity, and debug and improve code written by others, including AI-generated and partner code.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience at a SaaS product company (multi-tenant architecture, subscription products).

Experience working with or reviewing the work of contract or outsourced development teams.

IoT, connected equipment, or industrial and manufacturing data experience.
Modern front-end frameworks (e.g., React, Angular, Blazor).
Experience building AI or LLM-powered features into products.
Agile/Scrum experience and familiarity with delivery metrics such as DORA.
Curiosity about welding, fabrication, and the people who do the work.

description:

Primary Function of Position:
The Business Process Lead, FP&A Transformation is the enterprise process owner for how forecasting is designed, executed, and continuously improved at Intuitive. This high-impact individual contributor will lead the transformation of legacy, manual, and fragmented workflows into a simpler, faster, and more accurate forecasting operating model. Working with FP&A leadership across the organization, this role translates business needs into scalable processes, aligns stakeholders, pilots improvements, and drives sustained adoption.
The successful candidate is a systems thinker, process architect, and change leader who creates clarity in ambiguity, challenges unnecessary complexity, and connects process design to measurable outcomes. Success will be reflected in a forecasting model that is faster, simpler, more accurate, well governed, and consistently adopted across FP&A. Innovative thinking to challenge the current state to fully transform the forecast process.
Role and Responsibilities:
Diagnose and Design: Map end-to-end forecasting workflows, handoffs, decision points, rework loops, and elapsed-time gaps.
Identify root causes related to ownership, decision rights, data readiness, calendar design, and manual workarounds.
Design the future-state operating model, including workflow sequencing, inputs and outputs, decision gates, escalation paths, and integration points.
Prioritize, Pilot, and Scale: Build a transformation roadmap that sequences process, data, and automation opportunities by value, feasibility, risk, readiness, and dependencies.
Facilitate prioritization decisions with Finance leadership and clearly communicate trade-offs.
Design and lead pilots with defined scope, success measures, timelines, and learning objectives.
Measure outcomes, refine the approach, and scale proven changes while maintaining process integrity.
Track adoption and outcomes using measures such as cycle time, rework, compliance, engagement, and forecast accuracy trends.
Establish feedback loops and governance to sustain improvements.
Required Skills and Experience:
8+ years of progressive experience in business process excellence, finance transformation, FP&A operations, or a related discipline.
Experience partnering with Data, Systems, or Technology teams without directly owning technical delivery.
Success leading enterprise-scale process redesign from diagnosis through future-state design, pilot, rollout, and adoption.
Expertise with AI/ML-enabled forecasting and responsible integration of model outputs into financial processes.
Experience translating ambiguous problems into process blueprints, RACIs, decision gates, requirements, and prioritized roadmaps.
Lean Six Sigma, BPM, Design Thinking, or formal change management training or certification.
Proficiency with process-mapping tools such as Visio, Lucidchart, or Miro.
Hands-on experience facilitating process mapping and cross-functional working sessions.
Executive communication skills for VP- and C-suite audiences.
This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week.
Required Education and Training:
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Operations, Data Analytics, Information Systems or a related field.
Preferred Skills and Experience:
FP&A transformation experience, including forecasting operating model redesign, planning-cycle optimization, or driver-based planning.
Ability to influence without authority across senior leaders, business owners, and technical teams.
Strong analytical capabilities and experience evaluating transformation outcomes.
Experience in a publicly traded technology or medical-device company and a SOX-compliant environment.
