If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Position Summary
The Quality Assurance Manager, Audits & Inspections is responsible for the planning, execution, management, and continuous improvement of the company’s GxP audit and regulatory inspection readiness programs supporting late-stage pharmaceutical development.
The role provides hands-on leadership for internal, external, vendor, and study-related audits and establishes a sustainable inspection-readiness program as the organization progresses through Phase 3 clinical development toward regulatory submission, pre-approval inspection, and commercialization readiness.
Working under the direction of the Head of Quality Assurance, the Manager partners with Clinical Operations, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Nonclinical, and other functional teams to identify compliance risks, assess inspection readiness, manage audit observations and corrective actions, and ensure the organization and its critical service providers remain prepared for regulatory inspection.
This is a hands-on individual-contributor role requiring demonstrated experience conducting GxP audits and supporting FDA and/or other health-authority inspections.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Program Management
Develop and maintain a risk-based annual and multi-year GxP audit program covering internal functions, clinical studies, CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, pharmacovigilance providers, and other critical GxP vendors.
Plan, schedule, conduct, document, and close GxP audits in accordance with approved procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.
Develop audit plans, agendas, checklists, reports, observations, and follow-up documentation.
Evaluate audit observations for regulatory significance, systemic risk, and potential impact on product quality, subject protection, data integrity, and regulatory submissions.
Track audit findings, commitments, CAPAs, and effectiveness activities through closure.
Perform audit trending and provide periodic reporting of significant findings and emerging compliance risks to QA leadership.
Regulatory Inspection Readiness
Develop and maintain the company’s inspection-readiness program for FDA and other applicable health authorities.
Support readiness for BIMO, GCP, GMP, GLP, GVP and, as applicable, Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Conduct inspection-readiness assessments, mock inspections, document reviews, interview preparation, and functional readiness exercises.
Identify potential inspection vulnerabilities and coordinate remediation activities with responsible functional owners.
Maintain inspection-readiness tools, procedures, playbooks, request-management processes, and supporting documentation.
Support development and maintenance of inspection war-room, document-request, response-review, escalation, and communication processes.
Regulatory Inspection Management
Support the Head of Quality Assurance in coordinating and managing regulatory inspections.
Facilitate inspection logistics, document requests, SME preparation, inspection-room activities, and real-time issue escalation.
Review proposed responses and supporting evidence for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and regulatory defensibility.
Support evaluation and response to inspection observations, including FDA Form 483 observations and comparable health-authority findings.
Track post-inspection commitments and associated CAPAs through completion and effectiveness verification.
Vendor and Partner Quality Oversight
Conduct qualification, routine, for-cause, and risk-based audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, and other GxP service providers.
Evaluate vendor audit findings in the context of sponsor oversight responsibilities and program risk.
Partner with functional owners to establish appropriate remediation and escalation plans.
Support vendor qualification and ongoing performance monitoring based on audit results, quality events, compliance history, and risk.
Compliance Risk & CAPA
Identify emerging or systemic compliance risks through audit findings, inspection trends, quality events, and other quality intelligence.
Support or lead root-cause investigations associated with significant audit and inspection findings.
Review CAPAs for adequacy, proportionality, sustainability, and regulatory defensibility.
Perform or coordinate CAPA effectiveness verification associated with audit and inspection observations.
Escalate significant compliance risks promptly to the Head of Quality Assurance.
Cross-Functional Quality Partnership
Serve as a hands-on QA resource to functional teams preparing for audits and regulatory inspections.
Provide training and coaching to employees and SMEs regarding inspector interactions, documentation practices, inspection conduct, and response expectations.
Collaborate with QMS and GxP QA program functions to translate audit and inspection findings into sustainable improvements to the Quality Management System.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity when conducting audits and evaluating compliance.
Promptly escalate requests requiring significant regulatory interpretation, acceptance of material compliance risk, or final compliance disposition to the Head of Quality Assurance before communicating a final QA position.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, chemistry, engineering, or another relevant discipline.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or regulated life-sciences Quality Assurance experience.
Demonstrated hands-on experience planning, conducting, documenting, and closing GxP audits.
Experience conducting audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, clinical sites, or other regulated service providers.
Demonstrated experience supporting FDA or other health-authority regulatory inspections.
Strong working knowledge of applicable FDA regulations, ICH guidance, and GxP requirements.
Experience with audit observations, investigations, CAPA development, remediation, and effectiveness verification.
Strong technical writing skills and ability to produce clear, evidence-based audit reports and compliance assessments.
Ability to independently evaluate complex compliance issues and appropriately escalate significant risks.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting Phase 3 and late-stage pharmaceutical development.
Experience preparing for or supporting FDA BIMO and/or Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Cross-functional auditing experience spanning GCP, GMP, GLP, and/or GVP.
Experience with clinical-stage organizations operating through outsourced CRO/CDMO models.
Experience developing or implementing formal inspection-readiness programs.
Lead Auditor certification, ASQ certification, RQAP, or comparable professional credential is desirable but not required.
Key Competencies
The successful candidate should demonstrate strong auditor judgment and independence, exceptional attention to detail, regulatory and compliance acumen, concise technical writing, effective interviewing skills, and the ability to distinguish between isolated procedural deficiencies and systemic compliance risk. The individual must be comfortable challenging conclusions when warranted while maintaining productive working relationships with operational teams.

title: Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer - Future Forward
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
The Future Forward group within Intuitive Surgical is searching for a Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer to architect, design, and bring up the electronic hardware behind next-generation robotic and vision systems. This role is an exciting opportunity to join a small and innovative team in the early phases of product development, where design decisions made at the schematic and architecture level shape the performance of the entire system.
Joining Intuitive Surgical means joining a team dedicated to using technology to benefit patients by improving surgical efficacy and decreasing surgical invasiveness, with patient outcomes as our highest priority. The Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer owns analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuit design from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, design verification, and transfer to manufacturing. The ideal candidate designs for electromagnetic compatibility and signal integrity from the first block diagram rather than after the first chamber failure, and can isolate the most difficult board-level and system-level failures on the bench. A strong sense of integrity, care, and attention to detail is required, together with a commitment to developing products of the highest quality.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Design analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, and transfer to manufacturing.
Lead schematic and design reviews, and guide PCB layout for signal integrity, power integrity, and manufacturability.
Design for EMC and EMI from the start through grounding, shielding, filtering, isolation, and ESD protection, and support pre-compliance and compliance testing.
Bring up and debug prototypes in the lab, and drive hardware issues to root cause and a verified fix.
Integrate sensors, cameras, illumination, motor drives, and compute platforms in partnership with Mechanical, Firmware, Software, Vision, and Test teams.
Document designs, verification protocols, and results under Intuitive design controls.
Mentor engineers and help shape design practices, reference designs, and the technology roadmap for future products.
Drive external suppliers and design partners for camera, sensor, optics, and PCBA subsystems, setting technical direction and holding builds to schedule and quality targets.
Skills/Job Requirements:
Minimum 8 years' experience designing production electronics in the medical device, automotive, or robotics industry, including at least one product taken from concept to production.
Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science; a Master of Science degree preferred.
Strong schematic design, review, and debug skills across analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits, using Altium Designer, Cadence OrCAD/Allegro, or Siemens Xpedition.
Practical EMC and EMI design and troubleshooting experience, with working knowledge of standards such as IEC 60601-1-2, CISPR 11/32, or the IEC 61000-4 immunity series.
Solid signal integrity and power integrity fundamentals for high-speed interfaces such as MIPI CSI-2, LVDS, PCIe, USB, DDR, or Ethernet, including impedance control, return paths, crosstalk, and decoupling.
Direct experience with imaging and vision hardware, motor drive electronics, or precision sensing, and with transferring designs into manufacturing and production test.
Confident in the lab with oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, near-field probes, and logic or protocol analyzers, working with embedded interfaces such as I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, USB, and Ethernet, and using Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis.
Experience under a regulated quality system such as ISO 13485, FDA 21 CFR Part 820, IEC 60601-1, and ISO 14971, or automotive functional safety such as ISO 26262, is desired; FPGA design experience with VHDL or SystemVerilog is a plus.
Clear communication, strong documentation habits, and the ability to lead technical decisions, work independently, and mentor others.

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of the Position
Contribute your technical mechanical, manufacturing, and problem-solving skills to a dynamic team creating precision instruments for the daVinci SinglePort (SP) platform. This highly skilled mechanical engineer will support manufacturing lines for both mature and new products. Responsibilities include providing daily support for existing manufacturing lines, continuous improvement efforts, as well as developing manufacturing equipment and assembly processes for new products.
Essential Job Duties
Sustain and improve existing manufacturing lines: Provide daily engineering support for existing in-house manufacturing lines.
Own and drive continuous improvement of mechanical fixtures and processes to improve product quality, throughput, and cost. Utilize objective data and statistical analysis to inform and drive decisions.
Ideate, prototype, and implement simple, robust mechanical fixtures and tooling designed to error-proof complex assembly steps, take operator skill levels and manual technique out of the equation, and maximize production repeatability.
Lead root cause investigations and drive dispositions for assembly-related defects using Product and Process FMEAs as guidance.
Support quality system compliance including ECO review and implementation, discrepant material dispositions, nonconformance evaluations, and quality notifications.
Troubleshoot, resolve, and document equipment and process malfunctions in compliance with GXP and Intuitive Quality System requirements.
Assist in line transfer and line duplication activities.
Support implementation of design improvements to existing products, including: Provide feedback to Design Engineering on Design for Manufacturability/Assembly (DFM/DFA)
Lead Design Verification and Validation (V&V) builds
Coordinate cut-in/implementation in production.
Provide manufacturing feedback for supplier change requests (SCRs).
Support equipment and process qualification efforts (IQOQPQ and PPQs)
Contribute to the development of efficient manufacturing lines for New Product Introduction for medical devices for the daVinci SinglePort platform: Design and implement assembly/test fixtures to increase repeatability of complex assembly operations including cable routing, plastics joining (e.g. ultrasonic welding, heat staking, snap fit, press fit), metals joining (e.g. laser welding, riveting, swaging, crimping), and general assembly
Develop, document, and qualify (IQ/OQ/PQ/PPQ) new manufacturing and test processes using statistical tools such as Design of Experiments (DOE), Process Capability (Cpk), and Test method validation.
Specify and refine BOMs, workflows/travelers, and detailed work instructions.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (e.g. Production, Design Engineering, Quality Engineering, Supplier Engineering, Project Management) to meet project objectives including Design Verification & Validation and product launch. Examples include building prototype assemblies, training operators, identifying fixtures/tooling needed and conducting process validation.
Create and revise manufacturing-related risk documents including Process FMEAs, Manufacturing Line Specifications, Equipment Specifications.
Leadership Responsibilities: Leads/participates in continuous improvement initiatives focused on material cost reduction, capacity enhancement, and streamlining continuity of material supply.
Mentors and sets project tasks for Manufacturing Engineers on their specific project team, and on other teams as needed, to further company expertise & effectiveness.
Establish milestones, support, and success criteria for responsible projects.  Drive decisions and escalate key issues quickly maintaining stakeholder alignment.
Keep the organization’s vision and values at the forefront of decision-making and action.
Required Skills and Experience
Advanced fixture and tooling design experience: Proven track record of designing complex mechanical fixtures and custom tooling for precision manufacturing environments.
Integration with standard equipment: Hands-on experience developing custom tooling designed for integration into standard manufacturing equipment (e.g., presses, crimpers, heat stakers, ultrasonic welders).
Strong mechanical aptitude and fundamentals: Deep knowledge of mechanical design principles, fabrication methods, precise material selection, and surface treatments to optimize tooling performance.
Advanced CAD, GD&T, and Analysis: Strong 3D modeling/CAD experience (SolidWorks preferred), expert application of Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T), Tolerance stack-up analysis, and proficiency in FEA modeling.
Foundation in design, fabrication, and assembly process development for complex mechanical assemblies.
Demonstrated understanding of component manufacturing processes such as injection molding, transfer molding, thermoforming, machining, stamping, and MIM.
Technical problem-solving skills with ability to identify root cause and drive corrective action (Fishbone, 8D Analysis)
Ability to employ statistical methods (Cpk, ANOVA, Design of Experiments) in data analysis for process development and problem-solving.
Effective communication skills (verbal, written, and presentation) and comfortable interacting with production technicians, product design engineers, planning, buyers, clinical engineers, and suppliers.
Able to travel periodically to suppliers or Intuitive manufacturing sites.
Required Education and Training
Minimum B.S. Mechanical Engineering or related technical discipline. M.S. preferred.
8+ years with a B.S or 6+ years with an M.S of experience as a process or manufacturing engineer supporting products with significant mechanical content.
Working Conditions
Abhility to lift, maneuver, and troubleshoot fixtures and tools
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience in mid-volume manufacturing of single-use devices or complex electro-mechanical assemblies is a plus.
Experience in medical device design controls and manufacturing (ISO 13485) is a plus.
Machine tool experience is a plus.

title: Sr. Simulation & Synthetic Data Engineer - Remote
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
About the Team
Future Forward Research — Synthetic Data, builds the simulation and data infrastructure that powers Intuitive's autonomous surgical capabilities.
The Role
You'll build the virtual surgical worlds and the data pipelines that train our perception and policy models. Day to day, that means designing simulation environments, generating large volumes of labeled synthetic data, and working with ML engineers to close the sim-to-real gap for robotic surgery. It's a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of 3D simulation, machine learning, and robotics.
What You'll Do
Design and build high-fidelity simulation environments for surgical tasks.
Generate scalable synthetic datasets including photo realistic imagery, segmentation masks, depth, optical flow, and kinematic state — and own their quality, versioning, and delivery.
Implement domain randomization and procedural scene generation to maximize sim-to-real transfer.
Model deformable soft-tissue physics, tool-tissue contact, and instrument kinematics that match Intuitive's platforms.
Partner with ML engineers to define task curricula, reward functions, and evaluation benchmarks.
Develop and refine sim-to-real transfer strategies, and validate simulated behaviors against benchtop phantoms and real systems.
Build reusable tools, APIs, and documentation so the broader team can spin up new tasks without deep simulation expertise.
What You Bring
We care more about real depth in a few of these than shallow coverage of all of them.
Strong software engineering. You write maintainable, tested code in Python, C++ and/or C#, and you're comfortable in a Linux / Git / Docker / GPU workflow.
Hands-on simulation or graphics experience. You've built things in a physics simulator, game engine, or rendering/VFX pipeline — robotics simulators, real-time engines, and offline graphics pipelines all count.
A feel for data and models. You've produced data that trained an ML model (or worked closely alongside that), and you understand how data quality and distribution show up in model behavior.
Working knowledge of 3D and physics fundamentals — coordinate frames, rendering, rigid-body and contact dynamics — enough to reason about why a simulated scene does or doesn't look and behave correctly.
You've likely spent several years building games, simulation, graphics, robotics, or data systems — but we're far more interested in what you've built than in a specific number on your résumé. If you don't check every box, we still want to hear from you. Strong candidates often come from autonomous driving, humanoid robotics, gaming, or VFX rather than surgical robotics specifically.
Education
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Graphics, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field — or equivalent practical experience.
An advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a related area is a plus, not a requirement. We've hired strong engineers from all paths, including self-taught backgrounds and industry work in games, VFX, or robotics.
Bonus Points
None of these are required — they're signals, not gates. Any one of them is a nice plus.
Deformable-object simulation: FEM, position-based dynamics, or differentiable physics
NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab
Surgical robotics simulation: ORBIT-Surgical, dVRK-based environments
Sim-to-real techniques: domain randomization, system identification, privileged learning, residual policies
Vision-language or vision-language-action models, and how simulation data supports them
Procedural/generative asset creation: NeRFs, Gaussian Splatting, or diffusion models
Distributed compute at scale: Ray, Kubernetes, Slurm, multi-GPU/multi-node
Medical imaging or surgical video pipelines
Publications or open-source work in simulation, graphics, robotics, or AI
Tools You Might Use
You won't touch all of these, and we don't expect you to walk in knowing them.
Category
Examples
Simulation engines
Unity, NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab, MuJoCo
Deformable physics
PhysX FEM, SOFA, DiSECt, NVIDIA Warp/Newton, PBD
Rendering & data
USD, Omniverse Replicator, Blender
Infrastructure
Docker, Kubernetes, Ray, Airflow, CUDA
What Success Looks Like in Your First Year
Simulation environments for several core surgical tasks are operational and integrated with the ML training pipeline.
Synthetic data delivers measurable model lift on targeted perception or policy metrics.
A quantitative sim-to-real correlation is established on benchtop phantoms.
Parallelized infrastructure reliably generates thousands of training episodes per hour with automated dataset delivery.
A reusable task-creation framework lets ML engineers define new surgical skills without deep simulation expertise.

Day

Advanced Solar Technician

The Chalk Bluff Solar Energy Center site is a 450 MW-AC power generation facility located at 6198 HWY 357 S, HETH, AR 72346.  The site consists of GE Flexinverter 1566 inverters, NEXTracker NX Horizon 4 trackers, Jinko Eagle JKM585N-72HL4-BDV, JKM590N-72HL4-BDV. description:
Role purpose. The Manager, Canada Cheese & Dairy will lead the procurement strategy and commercial management for the full Canadian Business Unit portfolio of Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix. The role is accountable for category value delivery, supplier strategy, supply continuity, cost competitiveness, cross-border compliance and cross-functional execution across maintenance, productivity and innovation workstreams. The Manager will connect the Canadian Business Unit with North American category experts, translate market and business requirements into a Canada-specific sourcing strategy, and ensure clear information flow between Procurement and Canadian Business Unit leadership. Job Description
Primary Responsibilities:
Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management • Own and execute end-to-end sourcing strategies for the Canadian Cheese and Dairy portfolio, including market analysis, supplier segmentation, sourcing events, negotiations, contracting, implementation and ongoing commercial governance. • Develop and maintain a multi-year Canada sourcing strategy aligned with North American category strategies while reflecting Canadian market dynamics, business priorities, regulatory requirements and supply-chain constraints. • Partner closely with North American category experts to leverage market intelligence, supplier relationships, sourcing scale and best practices, while maintaining clear accountability for Canadian Business Unit outcomes. • Lead complex and high-value negotiations, supplier award recommendations and contracting, ensuring appropriate cost, service, quality, capacity, flexibility and risk protections. • Develop and communicate a strong point of view on Canadian and North American cheese and dairy markets, including commodity drivers, manufacturing economics, capacity, trade flows, tariffs and regional supply-demand dynamics. • Ensure pricing, contracts, specifications, supplier records and sourcing decisions are accurate, current and compliant within relevant source-to-pay and business systems.
Canada Cheese & Dairy Portfolio Responsibilities • Lead procurement for Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix across the Canadian Business Unit, balancing cost, functionality, specification, service and supply requirements. • Provide portfolio-level governance across maintenance, productivity, innovation, reformulation, promotions, plant transitions, capacity changes and new business opportunities. • Partner with R&D, Quality, Manufacturing, Commercial, Finance, Materials Management and the Canadian Business Unit to define requirements, technical specifications, project economics and implementation timing. • Lead supplier and procurement readiness for innovations, renovations, reformulations, promotions, plant transitions, product maintenance and business continuity initiatives. • Assess and manage category complexity, including product specifications, lead times, minimum order quantities, yields, conversion economics, supplier capacity and cross-border supply lanes. • Build and maintain contingency strategies for critical materials, suppliers, manufacturing locations and logistics routes serving Canada.
Cross-Border, Quota, Tariff & CDC Managemen t • Own procurement coordination for cross-border cheese and dairy flows into and out of Canada, ensuring commercial plans reflect applicable quotas, tariffs, customs requirements and regulatory obligations. • Lead procurement management of Canadian Dairy Commission (CDC) requirements and related processes, working with internal and external experts to support compliant and cost-effective execution. • Monitor quota availability, tariff exposure and cross-border cost implications, incorporating these factors into sourcing decisions, budgets, supplier negotiations and risk assessments. • Coordinate with Trade Compliance, Legal, Finance, Logistics, customs brokers, suppliers and category experts to resolve cross-border issues and maintain continuity of supply. • Maintain clear governance, documentation and escalation paths for quota, tariff and CDC activities affecting the Canadian portfolio.
Forecasting, Inventory & Materials Management • Provide leadership and governance for coordination with Materials Management on forecasts, inventory policies, material requirements, lead times, capacity and availability across the Canadian portfolio. • Lead cross-functional resolution of supply disruptions, delivery issues, allocation constraints and inventory imbalances, with clear escalation, ownership and recovery plans. • Drive improvements in forecasting discipline, inventory visibility, supplier communication and working-capital performance in partnership with Mount Royal Planners, Materials Management and Finance.
Supplier Relationship & Performance Management • Own strategic relationships with key Cheese and Dairy suppliers serving the Canadian market. • Support the management of key Canadian Semi-Finished Goods suppliers, including Agropur and other strategic partners, in close alignment with the relevant North American category owners. • Define supplier strategies and performance expectations across cost, quality, service, delivery, capacity, innovation, sustainability and risk. • Lead strategic business reviews, negotiations, performance interventions, improvement plans and resolution of escalated commercial or supply issues. • Establish fit-for-purpose supply agreements, pricing mechanisms, service commitments, capacity protections and risk mitigations. • Develop a resilient, competitive and capable Canadian supply base, including qualification of alternatives and management of supplier concentration or dependency risks. • Build collaborative supplier relationships that enable innovation, continuous improvement, transparency and long-term value creation.
Canadian Business Unit Leadership & Stakeholder Management • Act as the principal Procurement partner for Cheese & Dairy within the Canadian Business Unit, aligning category strategies and sourcing actions with Business Unit priorities. • Participate in Canadian Business Unit Leadership Team sessions as the Cheese & Dairy Procurement representative. • Cascade relevant market, supplier, cost, supply, policy and project information into the Canadian Business Unit Leadership Team, and communicate decisions, priorities, risks and required actions back to Procurement and North American category teams. • Influence senior cross-functional stakeholders and resolve competing priorities across Procurement, Materials Management, Manufacturing, R&D, Quality, Finance, Commercial and the Canadian Business Unit. • Prepare and deliver monthly business updates to the Associate Director, Cheese & Dairy, covering market developments, category performance, productivity, supplier performance, inventory and supply risks, strategic decisions and next steps. • Represent the category in annual planning, productivity, innovation, risk and business review forums.
Project Management & Continuous Improvement • Lead cross-functional programmes related to productivity, innovation, portfolio maintenance, supplier transitions, specification changes, risk mitigation, supply continuity and process improvement for Canada. • Establish governance, milestones, resources, decision forums and escalation paths for priority category initiatives. • Drive improvements in procurement processes, category analytics, supplier performance management, contracting, forecasting, inventory coordination and cross-border execution. • Ensure compliance with procurement policies, sourcing governance, approval requirements, contracting standards, supplier due diligence and internal controls.
Expected Experience & Required Skills • Bachelor's degree in supply chain, operations management, finance, business, food science or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. • 4-6 years of progressive experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, category management, supply chain or a related commercial discipline; dairy, cheese, food ingredients, commodity or external manufacturing experience is strongly preferred. • Proven experience developing category strategies, leading complex sourcing events and negotiations, and managing high-value supplier relationships and long-term agreements. • Strong understanding of Canadian dairy or food ingredient markets, commodity and conversion cost drivers, supplier capacity, forecasting, inventory, working capital and supply risk management. • Knowledge of Canadian dairy trade and regulatory considerations, including quotas, tariffs, cross-border processes and CDC requirements, is ideal. • Demonstrated ability to translate broader regional or global category strategies into market-specific sourcing and execution plans. • Strong commercial and financial acumen, strategic judgement and analytical problem-solving capability. • Ability to influence senior stakeholders, lead cross-functional teams and communicate complex category, market and supply dynamics clearly to executive audiences. • Proven ability to manage multiple high-impact priorities in a fast-paced environment, with strong governance, accountability and execution discipline. • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office and familiarity with source-to-pay and enterprise systems such as SAP and Ariba. Job Description:
Position Summary
The Finance Engineering Manager serves as the primary finance business partner to the Engineering organization, providing financial leadership and governance across the capital investment portfolio. This role is responsible for ensuring capital projects are appropriately evaluated, validated, approved, and executed in alignment with approved business cases and company financial objectives.
The Finance Engineering Manager supports Site Finance Managers through advanced analytics, factory benchmarking, and value realization processes that drive operational performance and network productivity improvements. The role serves as a key link between Engineering, Operations, and Finance to ensure investments and improvement initiatives deliver sustainable business results.
Key Responsibilities
Capital Project Financial Governance
Partner with Engineering teams to evaluate, validate, and prioritize capital investment opportunities.
Develop, review, and challenge project business cases to ensure financial assumptions, risks, and expected returns are robust and well supported.
Ensure capital expenditure requests comply with company financial policies, approval requirements, and investment criteria.
Support the capital authorization and approval process, providing financial recommendations to leadership.
Monitor project execution against approved scope, budget, timelines, and financial commitments.
Project Performance Tracking & Analysis
Track capital project actual spending against approved budgets and forecasts.
Identify and communicate project variances, financial risks, and opportunities throughout project execution.
Establish reporting and governance processes to monitor project performance across the capital portfolio.
Analyze project outcomes and conduct post-implementation reviews to ensure expected benefits and returns are realized.
Site Finance Partnership & Factory Performance Leadership
Partner with Site Finance Managers to provide financial insights, analytics, and benchmarking that drive factory performance improvements across the manufacturing network.
Develop and maintain standardized performance metrics, productivity & spending reporting and operational KPI analysis to support decision-making at the site and network levels.
Develop and analyze site-level depreciation modeling, including Asset Under Construction data, to develop affordability targets and scenario planning.
Analyze manufacturing performance trends, including cost, productivity, labor, efficiency, waste, and throughput, identifying opportunities to improve financial and operational results.
Support Site Finance Managers in evaluating the financial impact of operational initiatives, productivity programs, and continuous improvement efforts.
Provide data-driven insights to help factories identify performance gaps and prioritize improvement opportunities.
Collaborate with Site Finance and Operations leaders to track and validate value realization from productivity and operational improvement initiatives.
Drive consistency in performance measurement, reporting methodologies, and value tracking across the manufacturing network.
Continuous Improvement
Partner with engineering and operational leaders to identify opportunities for improved capital efficiency and investment returns.
Benchmark project performance, investment metrics, and financial outcomes across manufacturing facilities.
Share best practices and lessons learned to improve future project selection, execution, and value realization.
Strategic Business Partnership
Act as a trusted advisor to Engineering leadership on capital allocation, investment strategy, and portfolio management.
Support long-term manufacturing and engineering strategies through financial analysis and scenario modeling.
Provide insights and recommendations to senior leadership regarding capital deployment and resource prioritization.
Foster strong cross-functional relationships among Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance teams.
Qualifications
Education
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, or related field required.
MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant professional certification preferred.
Experience
7+ years of progressive experience in Finance, FP&A, Manufacturing Finance, Capital Management, or Engineering Finance.
Experience supporting engineering, manufacturing, operations, or supply chain organizations.
Strong understanding of capital investment analysis, project governance, and financial modeling.
Experience managing large capital portfolios and cross-functional projects preferred.
Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities
Strong financial modeling and investment analysis capabilities, including NPV, IRR, payback, and ROI methodologies.
Knowledge of manufacturing operations and capital project management processes.
Ability to influence decision-making across multiple levels of the organization.
Excellent analytical, communication, and presentation skills.
Strong project management and organizational abilities.
Ability to translate complex financial concepts into actionable business recommendations.
Advanced proficiency in financial systems, ERP platforms, and Microsoft Office applications.
Success Measures
Success in this role will be measured by:
Capital projects delivered within approved budgets and business case expectations.
Accuracy of project forecasts and financial tracking.
Achievement and validation of approved project savings and productivity targets.
Consistency of capital project valuation methodologies across the network.
Improved capital efficiency and return on investment.
Effective partnership and support of Engineering and Site Finance teams.
Timely identification and mitigation of project financial risks.
This role plays a critical part in ensuring the company's capital investments create sustainable value and support long-term manufacturing excellence.

title: Grinding Utility Operator - Nights
description:
Job Description:
Job Opportunity: Grinding Utility (Military & Veteran Friendly)
Shift: Nights (6pm - 6:30am) 223 Schedule
Location: Royal Canin, Fremont, NE
About Us
Royal Canin is seeking a Grinding Utility to join our exciting pet food business at our Fremont, NE manufacturing plant. We focus on the unique needs of cats and dogs. Our obsession with detail allows us to deliver precise, effective nutrition and help them become their magnificent best.
As part of our overall total compensation package, Royal Canin offers a competitive benefits package to all associates: Medical, Dental, Vision & Life Insurance, Short- & Long-Term Disability, and 401k match. Associates are also immediately eligible (based on hire date) for up to three weeks of vacation, 12 Paid Holidays per year, Sick Pay, Maternity & Parental Leave, and annual bonus earning potential, plus many other ancillary benefits not listed here.
Role Purpose & Military Value
The Grinding Utility role functions as a member of an area team that is directly responsible for the efficient production of quality products in the required quantities. This is a high-autonomy, leadership-oriented role where you will operate/change over specified machinery, coordinate shifts, and manage daily crewing needs—frequently without direct supervision.
We highly value the leadership, technical troubleshooting, shift coordination, and peer-training skills of military Non-Commissioned Officers (NCOs), Petty Officers, and technical specialists. If you have experience managing watch bills, crew assignments, equipment maintenance, or training junior service members, your skills are directly transferable here.
Key Responsibilities
Autonomous Leadership: Provide operational leadership and shift coordination for full shifts or multiple process areas, often without a production supervisor assigned (analogous to Tactical Operations/Watch Standing).
Crewing & Scheduling: Address daily crewing needs and shift schedule changes for optimized operation using planning skills and Staffing Tools (analogous to managing Watch Bills, Duty Rosters, or Section Staffing).
Production & Efficiency: Meet or exceed plant productivity goals by directing operational needs, staffing, and inventories.
Equipment Operation & Troubleshooting: Safely and efficiently operate pet food manufacturing equipment. Monitor production lines, identify faults, and immediately escalate complex downtime to Maintenance or QA.
Resource Coordination: Facilitate clear communication and planning with other leads/operators to ensure seamless shift changeovers, minimize downtime, manage waste, and ensure all ingredients and supplies are prepared.
On-the-Job Training: Conduct structured training and peer guidance for new associates on safety requirements, technical equipment operation, quality systems, and sanitation (analogous to Unit/Section Training and Certification).
Conflict Resolution & Team Building: Successfully resolve operational challenges and conflicts by listening, sharing information, and fostering a high-performing, positive team climate.
Reporting: Ensure all process logs, quality reports, and shift documentation are completed accurately, legibly, and on time.
Physical Requirements & Working Environment
Standing on a concrete floor for extended periods.
Wearing proper personal protective equipment (PPE) at all times (hair net, bump cap, ear plugs, safety shoes, and uniform).
Bending, stooping, twisting, turning, reaching, climbing stairs, and regularly lifting up to 55 lbs.
Adaptability to environmental and temperature extremes (hot/cold climates, dust, dirt, and food-safe chemicals).
Vision correctable to 20/20.
Qualifications & Experience
Minimum Requirements:
Be 18 years of age or older.
Have a High school diploma, GED, or equivalent.
Must be willing and able to work and accept varying shifts and schedules (night shift focus).
Ability to understand and effectively communicate in the English language.
Preferred Skills & Experience (Civilian or Military Equivalent):
Machine Operation: 1 year of experience operating machinery or managing technical systems (e.g., motor pool, aviation support, electrical/mechanical systems).
Technical Discipline: 1 year of experience in manufacturing, mechanical repair, trade discipline, or tactical equipment maintenance.
Logistics & Inventory: Familiarity with inventory control principles.
Equipment Certification: Ability to operate (or learn to operate) a Forklift and Scissor Lift.
Computer Literacy: Competency in computer and PC software (MS Office, email, spreadsheets).
What can you expect from Mars?
Work with over 130,000 like-minded and talented Associates, all guided by The Five Principles.
Join a purpose-driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
Best-in-class learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
An industry-competitive salary and benefits package, including company bonus.
Military Occupational Crosswalk
If you served in any of the following roles, your skills map directly to the Grinding Utility position:
U.S. Army
Combat Arms NCOs (11B, 19D, 13B - E5 and above): Highly transferable strengths in leading shifts, managing crew safety, coordinating complex schedules, and conducting peer-level training.
Wheeled Vehicle / Maintenance Supervisors (91B, 91X): Highly transferable strengths in technical equipment troubleshooting, equipment setup, preventive maintenance, and team safety leadership.
Logistical & Unit Supply Specialists (92A, 92Y): Highly transferable strengths in crew coordination, inventory control, and operating materials handling equipment (Forklift).
U.S. Marine Corps
Combat Arms NCOs (0311, 0321, etc. - E4 and above): Highly transferable strengths in independent decision-making, direct shift accountability, safety compliance, and team training.
Motor Transport Maintenance/Operations Chiefs (3529, 3537): Highly transferable strengths in managing daily crew schedules, overseeing equipment readiness, and managing shift workflows.
Supply Administration & Logistics (3043, 3051): Highly transferable strengths in tracking control systems, warehouse logistics, safety standards, and stock distribution.
U.S. Navy
Machinist's Mate / Gas Turbine Technicians (MM, GSM): Highly transferable strengths in complex mechanical operations, watch/shift leadership, troubleshooting, and strict checklist compliance.
Boatswain's Mate / Petty Officers (BM): Highly transferable strengths in crew leadership, coordinating watch bills, safety supervision, and direct hands-on training.
Logistics Specialists (LS): Highly transferable strengths in operating forklifts/MHE, database documentation, inventory, and shift-to-shift handoffs.
U.S. Air Force
Tactical Aircraft / Armament Maintenance (2A, 2W Series): Highly transferable strengths in handling complex mechanical machinery, high-attention to safety, shift-level coordination, and peer evaluations.
Materiel Management (2S0X1): Highly transferable strengths in inventory database systems, managing stock controls, and material handling equipment.
Pavements and Construction Equipment (3E2X1): Highly transferable strengths in forklift and scissor lift operation, civil engineering logistics, and safety plan execution.

title: Integrated Content Director
description:
Job Description:
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for a Integrated Content Director  to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food maker with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. Founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry across three major geographic regions.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here's the Scoop – Summary
The Integrated Content Director leads the strategy, planning and execution of content across the pet parent journey, ensuring brand strategy and communication priorities are translated into relevant, distinctive and effective content across channels and platforms.
This role owns integrated content planning, content governance, creative operations, production planning, agency coordination and content effectiveness, establishing the processes and ways of working required to deliver high-quality content with greater speed, agility and efficiency.
Working closely with Brand, Media & Digital, Ecommerce, Shopper Marketing, and partner agencies, the Director ensures content is fit for platform, connected across touchpoints and optimized for the moments that matter, while leveraging emerging technologies and AI-enabled creative solutions to accelerate content development and improve marketing effectiveness.
The Integrated Content Director  works out of our Corporate office in Boulder (CO), Nashville (TN) or New York (NY) and works a hybrid schedule with 3 days in-person.
What a typical day looks like:
Integrated Content Strategy & Planning. Lead the development and execution of integrated content strategies, translating brand communication platforms and portfolio/innovation priorities into clear content plans across the pet parent journey.
Content Ecosystem & Omnichannel Activation. Define how content comes to life across paid, owned, earned, social, retail, ecommerce and advocacy touchpoints, ensuring content is connected while being tailored to the role, audience and requirements of each channel.
Content Governance & Brand Consistency. Establish content governance principles, standards and ways of working to ensure consistency with brand strategy, visual identity, claims and communication guidelines while enabling effective local execution.
Creative Operations & Workflow Management. Own the end-to-end content workflow, from briefing and prioritization through creative development, approvals, production and deployment, simplifying processes and improving speed, visibility and accountability.
Agency & Creative Partner Leadership. Lead relationships and ways of working with creative, production and content partners, establishing clear scopes, expectations and performance standards while driving quality, efficiency and creative excellence.
AI-Enabled Content & Creative Transformation. Accelerate adoption of AI-enabled creative and content solutions to increase speed, agility, personalization and cost efficiency, while establishing appropriate governance and quality standards.
Fit-for-Platform Content Excellence. Champion the development of content designed for the specific behaviors and requirements of each platform, ensuring creative is relevant to the audience, channel and moment rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all approach.
Content Measurement & Effectiveness. Establish clear content effectiveness principles and measurement frameworks, using performance data, testing and learnings to continuously improve creative quality, relevance and business impact.
What are we looking for?
10+ years of progressive experience in Content Strategy, Integrated Marketing, Creative Operations, Brand Communications or related disciplines, ideally within consumer products, retail, ecommerce or consumer-facing organizations.
Strong expertise in integrated content strategy and planning , with demonstrated ability to translate brand and communication strategies into effective content ecosystems across multiple channels and platforms.
Strong digital-first orientation , with an understanding of platform-specific creative requirements, changing consumer behaviors and the increasing role of content in search, social commerce and digital discovery.
Demonstrated experience managing creative agencies, production partners and content ecosystems , including scopes of work, budgets, timelines and performance accountability.
Proven experience leading creative operations and production , including briefing, workflow management, asset development, approvals, production planning and deployment across complex organizations.
Strong knowledge of content governance and brand management , with experience establishing standards and processes that balance brand consistency with speed and local/channel relevance.
Experience with AI-enabled creative and content technologies .
Strong analytical orientation , with experience using content performance, testing and insights to optimize creative effectiveness and inform future development.
Strong cross-functional leadership and influencing skills
Proven people leadership experience , with the ability to develop talent, build capabilities and foster a high-performing, collaborative content culture.
What can you expect from Champion?
Safety:  a strong commitment to ensure all people are provided with a safe, healthy and respectful environment.
Earnings:  Salary range from USD$129,000 to USD$177,000, 401k with Company, and donation matching.
Industry Competitive Benefits:  Medical, Dental, Vision and Employee Assistance Programs to meet your individual or family needs.
Continuing Education:  In House & Online Learning & Development, as well as an Education Assistance Program.
Quality:  a dedication to uphold the highest standards of authenticity, nutritional integrity, and food safety, to earn the trust of Pet Lovers everywhere.
Other Perks:  Free Bag of Premium Pet Food each month, Free Parking and more!
What are you waiting for? Join the pack!
Come as you are.
We value diversity in all forms and know the power it can bring. Workplace equality allows for creative ideas to bloom, diverse points of views to be heard, and increases overall happiness. That sounds pretty good to us.
Champion is an equal opportunity employer. Regardless of your race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age, veteran status, or any other creed, you are wanted here.

This manager will implement and enforce established policy and area and organizational strategies.

Conversion - Manage the efforts of operating teams of a multi-line, area, or technology on one shift in efficiently converting materials into quality products in a safe, secure, and sanitary manner within the product design specifications.
Change Agent - Implement changes in methods, equipment, systems, and organization, as needed, to ensure that the objectives of the line/area are met and give input and recommendations for such changes by using a continuous improvement mindset.
Mars Supply Excellence – Lead or participate in one or more MSE Pillars; Lead and support the implementation of Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs) in area of responsibility; Lead key connection points and own reliablity data collection accuracy.
Area Ownership – Collaborate with the rest of the Area Leadership Team (Area Manager or Continuous Improvement Engineer, Continuous Improvement Specialist, Maintenance Coordinator) to create and execute the reliability strategy for the area of responsibility.
Coaching – Coach operators to build their functional and leadership capabilities and to drive accountability in safety, Quality and Food Safety, Autonomous Maintenance, and team engagement.
Line Operations - Coordinate materials, staffing and resources to support line operation and changeovers.
Standards Implementation and Adherence – Ensure standards are implemented on shift and in areas of responsibility through effective communication, change management, consistent reinforcement, and coaching, guidance, and accountability measures.
Associate Safety – Ensure safe working conditions, behaviors, and mindsets through the direct implementation of Mars Safety programs and driving a relentless focus among a team of operators.
Food Safety and Product Quality – Ensure the ongoing production of safe and defect-free products consistent with the principles of Mars.  HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
Associate Advocacy - Manage associate relations issues and guide and direct the hiring, training, retraining, development, and motivation of Operations associates following self-managed, team-working principles with a minimum degree of guidance from the Area Manager or Value Stream Manager.

Goal Setting and Measurement - With the general guidance of the Value Stream or Area Manager and/or the support of the Continuous Improvement Engineer, establish line and individual performance standards and goals, and measure, control, take corrective action, and report results as appropriate.
Troubleshooting – Utilize the technical resources on shift for the preventive maintenance, repair and troubleshooting of process/packaging equipment problems, to effectively use these resources to achieve desired performance levels.
Escalations - Proactively identify risks and opportunities and reactively lead on-shift incident resolution when operators require additional support. Prioritize, assign resources against escalated issues, and make decisions to resolve escalated issues.
Communications - Ensure that open communications are established and that opportunities to broaden the scope and responsibility of Operations teams/associates are undertaken.
Technology Advancement - Advise when opportunities exist for moving the line/area forward in technological change.
Operations Strategy - Participate in implementing improvement strategies to help the line/area perform more effectively in the near term.
Recruiting and Onboarding – Responsible for partnering with Talent Acquisition to recruit and select associates for operations roles, and responsible for onboarding associates effectively.
Associate Development – Develop associates by mentoring and supporting their development plans and helping them grow in functional capability and long-term career.

The equivalent experience is defined as greater than four years of experience in a technical manufacturing continuous improvement environment, along with a High School Diploma.

A degree in one of the Engineering, basic sciences, or business-related disciplines.

Experience and demonstrated capability in leading others.
Previous direct people leadership experience preferred.
Working knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices.
Ability to convey communications clearly and concisely.
Understanding of major functions within the plant and the ability to work directly with all levels and functions.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office software (Word, Excel, etc), internet software, e-mail.
Ability to succeed in an ambiguous environment.
Functional knowledge and understanding of HACCP concepts.
Experience in plant sanitation practices and procedures.
Ability to deliver critical performance feedback and hold associates accountable to business objectives.

title: Editor, Research Team
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As Editor, Research, you will help define the editorial voice of OpenAI’s research films. You will personally edit films that introduce new models, demonstrate emerging capabilities, and tell the stories behind our research. You will lead the editorial approach across assigned projects, guide collaborators, and set a high standard for cinematic storytelling and craft.

Your influence will begin well before footage reaches the edit. Working alongside researchers, filmmakers, and production, design, and product partners, you will shape concepts, develop narratives, test ideas through prototypes, and help plan shoots and demonstrations with the finished film in mind. You will bring clarity, humanity, and emotional depth to complex, evolving subjects, finding compelling ways to show the research while preserving its meaning and technical accuracy.

This is a hands-on leadership role for an exceptional editor who makes the work—and the people around them—better. You will take responsibility for editorial execution from concept through delivery, provide clear creative direction and actionable feedback, mentor editors, and lead external collaborators. You will also strengthen shared workflows and practices that help the studio deliver ambitious work across formats, platforms, markets, and timelines.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Lead editorial work from concept through final delivery, personally editing research launch films, cinematic demonstrations, and stories about the people behind the work while directing the contributions of other editors on assigned projects. Take responsibility for narrative quality and continuity across development, production support, editing, finishing, and delivery.

 - Set editorial direction across assigned projects, translating creative goals into a clear approach and helping internal editors and external partners deliver cohesive, distinctive work. Bring exceptional judgment to story, structure, pacing, performance, music, sound, and the relationship between picture and graphics.

 - Shape stories from the beginning, partnering with filmmakers and researchers on concepts, treatments, scripts, interview questions, and demonstration coverage. Use rough cuts, story assemblies, and rapid prototypes to find the strongest narrative and inform what needs to be captured.

 - Lead editorial reviews, presenting work and explaining creative choices clearly. Synthesize feedback from researchers and creative partners into focused revisions that strengthen the film while preserving the accuracy of demonstrations and technical explanations.

 - Lead editors and editorial collaborators on assigned projects, setting clear expectations, delegating work, supporting onboarding, and providing actionable creative feedback. Mentor editors and assistant editors to strengthen their storytelling, technical skills, and independent judgment.

 - Partner with production to scope and deliver editorial work, assessing resource needs, estimating effort, setting realistic schedules, and recommending the right talent for each assignment. description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI Finance is responsible for ensuring the organization is set up for success in pursuit of its mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity.

 


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an accountant to own an assigned portfolio of intercompany and investment accounting processes. You will manage recurring reconciliations, coordinate the accounting for intercompany funding, review transfer pricing calculations and journal entries, and partner with Technical Accounting on investments. A fundamental part of the role is understanding OpenAI's group structure, partnering closely with Tax on complex transactions, and providing guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows.

You will own work from source data through close, resolve routine issues independently, and improve processes within established policies and approval controls. You will identify matters requiring technical assessment early and bring clear analysis and supporting facts for review. You will be a pivotal interface between global finance teams, treasury, tax, and systems to support our mission-critical financial close and reporting processes.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Develop and maintain an understanding of OpenAI's group structure, ownership relationships and intercompany arrangements and flows.

 - Partner with Tax, Technical Accounting and your manager to assess complex intercompany transactions and coordinate implementation of agreed accounting treatments.

 - Provide guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows, accounting treatments and cross-entity accounting questions.

 - Own monthly and quarterly close activities for assigned accounts, including reconciliations and resolution of reconciling items.

 - Coordinate accounting for intercompany funding and settlements with Treasury and Tax, within established approval and execution controls.

 - Review transfer pricing calculations prepared by the TP team for intercompany accounting accuracy, including entity, account, currency and FX rate treatment.

 - Prepare and review assigned journal entries for accuracy, supporting evidence and consistency with approved accounting treatments and controls.

 - Maintain investment accounting records and reconciliations, implement agreed accounting treatments, and partner with Technical Accounting and your manager on new transactions and technical assessments.

 - Maintain close and audit support, document processes and controls, and work with systems teams to improve accounting workflows and resolve reporting issues.


WHAT YOU WILL BRING

 - Experience owning recurring accounting work through close, including balance sheet reconciliations, journal entries, and investigation of reconciling items.

 - A working understanding of US GAAP and multi-entity accounting, with the judgment to distinguish routine application of established policy from matters that need technical review.

 - Familiarity with intercompany transactions, settlements, and foreign currency accounting. Experience with transfer pricing calculations or investment accounting is relevant to this role.

 - Careful review habits and the ability to trace a calculation or journal entry to its source, explain discrepancies, and document how they were resolved.

 - The ability to organize a close calendar, manage dependencies, and communicate clearly with Accounting, Treasury, Tax, and Technical Accounting. You follow through independently and raise issues with enough context for others to act.

 - Comfort working with spreadsheets and accounting systems. Experience with Oracle FCCS or a similar consolidation system, internal controls, or audit support would be useful.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Your assigned close activities are completed on time, with accurate entries and reconciliations that are easy to review.

 - Reconciling items are resolved promptly, and unresolved issues have clear owners and next steps.

 - Funding, transfer pricing, and investment accounting records reflect approved transactions and treatments, with complete supporting evidence.

 - Documented processes and practical improvements reduce rework, while complex or unusual matters reach your manager early enough for a considered decision.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Silicon Design Lead to drive architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of key IP and subsystems for our AI hardware platforms. You will translate functional, performance, and security requirements into efficient silicon designs, owning technical decisions from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

Part of this role will focus on hardware security implementation in close partnership with OpenAI’s Security team. While the Security team owns the overarching security architecture and requirements, you will translate those requirements into silicon microarchitecture and implementation, balancing security capabilities with performance, power, area, and design complexity. The other part of this role will focus on driving general silicon architecture/microarchitecture. 

In this role, you will:

 - Own architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of silicon IP and subsystems, from requirements and design specifications through integration and validation.

 - Define hardware interfaces, data flows, and microarchitectural tradeoffs to meet functional, performance, power, and area requirements.

 - Partner closely with OpenAI’s Security team to translate security architecture, requirements, and threat models into implementable hardware capabilities.

 - Design and integrate hardware security mechanisms, including encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, and data protection across silicon subsystems.

 - Evaluate architectural and implementation tradeoffs to ensure security capabilities meet functional and performance requirements.

 - Collaborate with silicon architects, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive subsystem design, integration, and validation.

 - Review and contribute to RTL implementations, ensuring designs align with architectural intent and system requirements.

 - Evaluate existing and third-party IP, identify architectural or implementation gaps, and drive solutions across subsystem boundaries.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have strong experience in silicon IP or subsystem-level architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation.

 - Have owned hardware IP or subsystem designs from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

 - Have experience implementing hardware security features such as memory encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, or secure boot.

 - Understand how to translate functional and security requirements into hardware architectures, interfaces, and microarchitectural specifications.

 - Have working knowledge of RTL design and coding proficiency in Verilog or SystemVerilog, with the ability to read, review, and contribute to RTL.

 - Can evaluate performance, power, area, and complexity tradeoffs across silicon designs.

 - Work effectively across security, silicon architecture, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive designs from concept through execution.

 - Ideally, have broader SoC-level architecture or integration experience, though deep IP or subsystem-level expertise is sufficient.

The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large-scale compute clusters that serve the models backing ChatGPT and the API, while also supporting training workloads for our next generation models. We operate a large, modern GPU fleet and provide a unified platform for other OpenAI teams to run production Applied AI and Research training workloads.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You will join the Compute Infrastructure TPM team as a Technical Program Manager for Capacity Analytics & Tooling. You will serve as the product manager for our supply and demand planning tools, owning the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of the systems teams use to forecast demand, understand supply, and plan allocations. Your users will include Product TPMs, Capacity TPMs, and Compute TPMs, alongside partners across Finance, Accounting, Leadership, Engineering, and Research.

This role combines product management, technical program leadership, data engineering, and applied data science. You will partner with engineering and data teams to build reliable data foundations, improve forecasting and scenario planning, and scale our tools and success metrics across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources. You will help teams make informed capacity decisions across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other infrastructure providers.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the product strategy and roadmap for supply and demand planning tools. Understand user needs, set priorities, define success measures, and guide delivery from initial requirements through adoption and ongoing improvement.

 - Build useful planning workflows. Translate complex processes into tools for demand intake, forecasting, supply tracking, scenario analysis, and allocation planning. Help teams understand what infrastructure they need, when it will be available, and which gaps require action.

 - Scale the data infrastructure behind capacity planning. Partner with engineering on ingestion, transformation, storage, and delivery of planning data. Guide technical tradeoffs as the number of resources, providers, data sources, and users grows.

 - Make planning data consistent and trustworthy. Establish shared data models and definitions for supply, demand, allocations, utilization, and cost. Drive data cleaning, validation, reconciliation, and traceability so users can understand and trust planning outputs.

 - Advance forecasting and analytical capabilities. Work with engineering and data partners to connect product and research plans to infrastructure demand. Make assumptions, uncertainty, forecast accuracy, and capacity constraints visible to decision makers.

 - Define and scale meaningful success metrics. Measure data quality, forecast performance, planning speed, and tool adoption. Establish consistent ways to track capacity availability, utilization, and efficiency across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources.

 - Support planning across multiple cloud providers. Build capabilities that account for differences in resource types, regions, availability, commercial commitments, and deployment constraints across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other providers.

 - Lead delivery across data, infrastructure, and planning teams. Manage dependencies, technical tradeoffs, migrations, risks, and releases. Keep teams aligned on priorities and the decisions needed to move work forward.

 - Drive adoption and reduce manual planning work. Develop simple workflows, documentation, training, and feedback mechanisms. Identify recurring reconciliation and reporting work that can be improved through better data and automation.

 - Make capacity tradeoffs clear to leadership and partner teams. Provide useful views of gaps between supply and demand, allocation options, and their financial and operational consequences. Partner with Finance and Accounting to align planning data with budgeting and reporting needs.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 5+ years of experience leading technical programs or products in data platforms, infrastructure, capacity planning, or a related field, with a record of delivering systems that teams rely on.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Research Compute Services builds the systems that help researchers use OpenAI’s compute fleet effectively. We partner with Research and Compute Infrastructure to support workloads across the compute stack, including pretraining, synthetic data generation, sampling, research inference, and reinforcement learning.

Our work connects changing research needs with capacity planning, allocation, and scheduling. We build tools and services that help researchers express their compute needs, access the right resources, and run their workloads effectively. As the fleet and our research ambitions grow, we continually improve how compute is planned, allocated, and used.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, partnering closely with the Research Compute Services team. Your primary responsibility will be to build and own the tools, data, and platform that turn Research plans and workload signals into concrete compute demand and manage allocations across the fleet.

This is a hands-on technical role. You will build alongside researchers and engineers, working directly with code and data to prototype solutions, automate workflows, and deliver tools that teams use every day. You will combine technical judgment and program leadership to connect capacity planning with the deployment, scheduling, and optimization systems that make allocated compute usable.

You will work across a broad range of Research workloads, understanding their different requirements and ensuring those needs shape the platform. Success means researchers can express their needs, understand their allocations, and use compute effectively as priorities and workloads change.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build with Research. Work directly with researchers across pretraining, research inference, and other workloads. Treat these communities as core users, and translate their needs into improvements across compute services, tooling, and scheduling.

 - Own Research demand and allocation systems. Own the roadmap and delivery of the tools, data, and platform used to capture demand, support allocation decisions, and manage allocations. Carry this work from requirements and design through adoption and ongoing improvement.

 - Connect allocations to workload execution. Partner with engineers working on Kubernetes deployments and scheduling systems so allocation plans reflect workload constraints and translate into resources that researchers can use.

 - Improve allocation and scheduling efficiency. Work with engineers to evaluate optimization approaches, including solvers operating at fleet and local scheduling levels. Help define constraints and objectives, assess tradeoffs, and measure improvements in fleet utilization.

 - Find and address systemic gaps. Use workload and fleet data to identify bottlenecks, unused capacity, and recurring manual work. Build durable improvements to the tools and systems behind those problems.

 - Make progress and tradeoffs clear. Give working teams and leadership a clear view of demand, allocation constraints, delivery progress, and decisions that need attention.

 - Have led and delivered complex technical programs involving large-scale compute, distributed systems, infrastructure platforms, or research environments.

 - Have practical experience with capacity planning, including supply and demand management, compute allocations, and the tools and data that support those decisions.

 - Have personally built or materially contributed to tools, data systems, or automation used by engineering or research teams. You are comfortable working directly with code and operational data.
