title: Senior Data Scientist, Hardware Quality
description:
Our mission at ŌURA is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
At Oura, our mission is to empower every person to own their inner potential. With our award-winning Oura Ring and app, we help millions of people turn insights about sleep, activity, and readiness into healthier, more balanced lives.We are looking for an experienced Senior Data Scientist to partner with Oura’s Hardware, Quality, Firmware, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Support Engineering, and Finance teams. This role will help build the data science and decision systems that make Oura hardware more reliable, from early product testing and launch readiness through field performance, warranty outcomes, and long-term product improvement.You will work on some of the most important problems in consumer hardware: understanding why products fail, predicting reliability before issues reach members, connecting manufacturing and testing data to field outcomes, and turning complex engineering data into clear decisions. This is a full-stack applied data science role that combines data foundations, statistical modeling, machine learning, experimentation, and cross-functional technical leadership.
What You Will Do:
Build and evolve reliability and quality models for current and next-generation Oura Ring products, including warranty forecasts, runtime degradation, survival analysis, failure-mode prediction, and cohort-based field-performance analysis.
Develop diagnostics and root-cause analysis systems that connect ring telemetry, firmware and engineering diagnostics, manufacturing records, supplier and component data, testing results, activations, and warranty outcomes.
Partner with Hardware, Quality, Firmware, Battery Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Support Engineering to identify the highest-leverage reliability risks and translate them into measurable analytical problems.
Analyze component, supplier, manufacturing-process, and ring-build variation to identify drivers of product quality and inform corrective actions, design decisions, and supplier-quality improvements.
Build trusted analytical data products and pipelines that unify hardware, manufacturing, firmware, diagnostic, activation, and warranty data and make them usable for recurring analysis and decision-making.
Develop production AI-enhanced dashboards, monitoring, and decision-support tools that surface emerging failure risks and provide clear, actionable recommendations to technical and executive stakeholders.
Establish robust measurement practices for hardware quality, including metric definitions, cohorting, normalization, uncertainty, data-quality checks, and appropriate statistical methods.
Translate complex technical findings into concise recommendations that influence hardware roadmaps, launch decisions, quality plans, firmware priorities, warranty strategy, and member experience.
Take end-to-end ownership of ambiguous, cross-functional problems and help raise the bar for data science practices through documentation, peer review, reusable tooling, and mentorship.
This is a remote US role with a slight preference for candidates based in San Francisco.
What you'll bring:
6+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, reliability engineering, quality analytics, or a closely related quantitative field, with a track record of owning high-impact problems end to end.
Demonstrated experience applying statistical modeling, machine learning, experimentation, or advanced analytics to reliability, quality, manufacturing, hardware, IoT, electronics, automotive, medical devices, or another physical-product domain.
Strong experience with reliability and time-to-event methods, such as survival analysis, hazard modeling, accelerated-life testing, degradation modeling, warranty forecasting, or related techniques.
Strong proficiency in SQL and Python, with experience building analytical data models, statistical or machine-learning workflows, and production-quality measurement systems.
Strong data-engineering intuition, including experience unifying and transforming data from multiple operational and technical systems into reliable datasets for analysis and modeling.
Experience working with noisy, incomplete, longitudinal, or high-volume telemetry and test data, and the judgment to distinguish data artifacts from meaningful product signals.
Experience designing experiments or observational analyses that support technical decisions, including an understanding of confounding, bias, uncertainty, and validation.
Experience with modern cloud and data platforms such as Databricks, AWS, dbt, Snowflake, or similar tools.
Proven ability to communicate complex analytical concepts clearly to engineers, quality and operations partners, product leaders, and executives.
Proven ability to work effectively across distributed, cross-functional teams and to drive progress when requirements and data are still evolving.
Nice to have:
Experience with consumer electronics, wearables, IoT, batteries, embedded systems, firmware, sensors, or connected devices.
Experience analyzing manufacturing, supplier, component traceability, MES, ERP, engineering test, or warranty data.
Experience with battery degradation, runtime modeling, charging optimization, power management, or electronics reliability.
Experience building field-failure analysis, anomaly detection, predictive-maintenance, or early-warning systems.
Familiarity with hardware development and launch processes, including EVT, DVT, PVT, and field-test programs.
Benefits

What we offer:
Competitive salary and equity packages
Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources
An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family
20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off
Paid sick leave and parental leave

title: General Manager - Site Operations
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE:

As the Site Leader, Warehouse at Quince.com, you will play a pivotal role in overseeing our fulfillment center operations, driving performance while fostering a positive and safe work environment within a rapidly growing business and a 100,000 square foot facility. Leading a dynamic team that includes two Operations Managers, two Area Managers, and up to 1,000 hourly Associates, you'll be responsible for budget management, people development, and achieving operational objectives. You will oversee daily operations, lead continuous improvement initiatives, and ensure exceptional customer satisfaction. This is a unique opportunity to shape the future of our operations and contribute to a collaborative, results-driven team culture.
Responsibilities
Lead and manage all aspects of site operations, including performance, quality, safety, and customer experience across inbound receiving, inventory management, and outbound fulfillment departments.

Ensure all safety standards and compliance regulations are followed, creating a secure working environment for all team members and minimizing incidents and injuries.

Cultivate positive employee relations, support career development, and promote a strong leadership pipeline within the organization.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (HR, Finance, IT, Facilities, Logistics) to ensure resource availability and support for key projects and initiatives.
Share best practices, operational innovations, and lessons learned with other facilities and headquarters to drive consistency and operational excellence across the network.
Manage the operational P&L for the site, ensuring cost control, budget adherence, and working capital efficiency.

7+ years of leadership experience in distribution, e-commerce fulfillment, or manufacturing environments, including at least 2 years in a senior management role

Ability to manage a diverse team and provide ongoing coaching and mentorship

Experience managing both salaried and hourly workforces in a large-scale distribution or fulfillment center

description:

Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
Join Our Team as a Component Quality Technologist!
The Component Quality Technologist is responsible for the inspection of individual components, both internally manufactured and externally sourced, to ensure they meet required quality standards. The role requires knowledge of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), the ability to read technical drawings, and the use of measuring equipment to confirm product conformity. The Technologist ensures that component defects are identified, documented, and resolved before components proceed further in the production process.
In this job you will be responsible for inspecting fabricated parts, sub-assemblies and final assemblies, including painted components, made from various machines such as shears, punch presses, and welding work centers. You will be required to work with assembly and detailed prints, industry standards, routings, BOMs, specifications, instruction bulletins, and customer notes. Inspecting the products will require you to use various pieces of inspection equipment and the ability to select the appropriate measuring equipment such as tape measures, go/no go gages, special gages, torque wrenches, thread plug gages, fluke meters, and fuses holder standards. The job will require you to clearly communicate verbally and in written format. Abnormal conditions, must be clearly recorded on the Checklist, DPU report, and/or on a NMR. All defects will be recorded and clearly explained to assembly team members and shop floor leadership. There will be times when product will be placed on hold until you clearly explain the abnormal conditions to engineers so they can determine if the product could be sent to the customer or needs to be reworked.
Key Responsibilities:
Perform detailed inspections of components to ensure they meet dimensional and material specifications.
Interpret technical drawings, BOMs, and GD&T to assess compliance with design requirements.
Record and document inspection results, including the identification of non-conforming materials.
Utilize, maintain, and calibrate precision measuring equipment, such as micrometers and calipers, to verify component dimensions.
Collaborate with procurement and production teams to address quality issues and suggest improvements to processes.
Assist in developing and improving testing procedures and protocols based on findings and feedback.
Understand and follow ISO 9001 standards and ensure compliance in daily work.
Maintain detailed inspection logs and reports for review by supervisors.
Assist in maintaining the safety of the work area by following relevant safety guidelines for handling mechanical components and equipment.
Continuously develop skills related to mechanical testing and inspection techniques, with a focus on pursuing relevant certifications (e.g., ASQ, ASME).
Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
Work with departmental mentors to gain and apply feedback in pursuit of improved work quality.
Other responsibilities as assigned.
What you’ll Need To Succeed:
3+ years of experience inspecting in a manufacturing environment .
Basic understanding of GD&T
Basic understanding of Metrology
MS Outlook skills.
Ability to use shop math.
Ability to read and understand mechanical drawings for fabricated parts, mechanical assemblies and specials.
Ability to use basic dimensional measuring tools. (mics, calipers, height gage, pins gages, threaded gages, measuring tape)
Ability to use a resistance meter.
Ability to maintain accurate records.
Ability to support departmental team members on short notice.
Ability to change your start times on short notice as needed.
Ability to work independently in a service-oriented environment.
Ability to clearly communicate verbally and in writing.
Ability to use a pallet jack and ladder safely.
Ability to inspect from elevated heights when necessary.
Willingness to learn software such as Oracle, Compliance Quest (QMS), Wriker, and SmarTeam
Ability to navigate to E-Docs and Operating System Documents on SharePoint or EVault.
Preferred:
An Associate degree or Certificate in a Technical Discipline
3+ years of hands-on manufacturing experience, such as assembly.
Sound understanding of mechanical systems and their components. Able to complete troubleshooting tasks to identify issues within these systems and their components.
Ability to understand part drawings, Bills of Material, Sales Orders, & Technical Documents.
Good understanding of ISO 9001.
Basic understanding of and ability to apply GD&T.
Willingness to work in a manufacturing environment on a product floor and open to learning new concepts of mechanical/product testing.
Proficient in performing precise and delicate tasks using hands and fingers. Able to manipulate small objects, operate tools, and handle intricate equipment effectively.
Sound attention to detail, with the ability to follow detailed instructions and identify correct vs. incorrect product functions.
Rounded communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to articulate information efficiently and effectively to team members in a variety of production support departments.
Good computer skills with the ability to review and respond to requests and use Microsoft/ERP applications.
Ability to use hand tools and precision measuring equipment.
Good shop math skills with the ability to calculate measurements.
Good interpersonal and organizational skills with the ability to understand and complete requests given by team members inside and outside of the department.
Ability and willingness to follow Health, Safety & Environment procedures accurately, reporting concerns promptly to the safety action team.
Experience working in an inspection role in a manufacturing organization.
Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement manufacturing principles.
MAJOR PHYSICAL DEMANDS
Standing: Most tasks performed in a standing position with frequent walking.
Lifting: Frequent lifting of items weighing up to 40 lbs.
Walking: Frequent walking short distances (total one to two miles)
Carrying: Frequent carrying of items weighing up to 40 lbs.
Pushing/Pulling: Frequent use of cart to transport material
Bending: Frequent bending and crouching required
Reaching: Occasional full range of motion from above the shoulders to below the knees

title: Manufacturing & Process Engineer
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

You'll own how Standard Bots robots get built — from the first process design to the last improvement on the production floor. Our factory is in Glen Cove, NY, and you'll be on it every day, so the fixture you design or the fix you make today shows up on the line tomorrow morning. The discipline we build now will define the quality and cost of every robot we ship, and you'll help set it.

This is an individual contributor role for an engineer who wants real ownership early. You'll report to the Manufacturing & Process Engineering Manager and work closely with product, mechanical engineering, quality, and production. As production scales, so will your scope.

📍 Location

You'll work on-site at our factory in Glen Cove, NY, five days a week.


What you'll do

- Sit in DFM/DFA reviews with product and mechanical engineering and bring concrete feedback on assemblability, tolerances, and cost, not vague opinions.

- Design, build, and validate the fixtures, tooling, and workstations used for robot assembly and test.

- Own the process flow for your assigned assemblies, and support NPI as new products move from prototype to production.

- Spot automation opportunities in assembly, test, and material handling, then build the case for the ones actually worth doing.

- Drive measurable gains in yield, cycle time, and first-pass quality on the stations and lines you own.

- Run root cause analysis on defects and nonconformances, put corrective actions in place, and verify they hold.

- Contribute to PFMEAs and control plans, and feed what you learn on the floor back into them.

- Use time studies, capacity analysis, and lean tools (5S/6S, standard work, value stream mapping) to cut waste.

- Write and maintain the work instructions, routings, and BOM accuracy for your processes.

- Track process metrics (capability, yield, cycle time) and report them weekly.


What you'll bring

- 3–5 years in manufacturing or process engineering in a hardware production environment.

- A bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field.

- Hands-on production-level experience with DFM/DFA, fixture design, and process documentation.

- CAD proficiency (SolidWorks, Onshape, or similar) for fixture and tooling design.

- Working knowledge of root cause analysis and lean or continuous improvement methods.

- At least one quality or throughput improvement you scoped, delivered, and can put a number on.

- Comfort on the shop floor every day, in a place where the playbook is still being written.


Nice to have

- Background in robotics, automation hardware, or complex electromechanical assembly.

- Exposure to scaling from low-volume prototype to higher-volume production.

- Experience with PFMEA, control plans, or SPC.

- Exposure to sheet metal, machined components, PCB assembly, or mixed-process manufacturing.

- Familiarity with MES, ERP, or manufacturing data systems.

- Basic scripting or data analysis skills (Python, SQL, or advanced Excel).


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $150,000 - $180,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

description:

About Stripe

Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Stripe’s Tax Transfer Pricing team designs, implements, and defends the intercompany pricing policies that support Stripe’s global operating model, ensuring pricing between Stripe entities is compliant, defensible, and aligned with how the business creates value.
As Stripe expands its product portfolio and international footprint, our transfer pricing policies and documentation must evolve alongside the business. Transactions between Stripe affiliates are becoming increasingly complex and, in some cases, share characteristics with transactions commonly undertaken by financial services institutions. These arrangements, including those supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities, may also be subject to scrutiny from regulators that oversee the financial services sector. We are seeking an experienced Transfer Pricing Specialist with financial services expertise to help develop practical, scalable transfer pricing policies, work through the tax and regulatory considerations relevant to intercompany arrangements, and provide subject matter expertise in audit defense and dispute resolution.
What you’ll do
The Financial Services Transfer Pricing Strategist will be a hands-on, collaborative member of the team responsible for developing and implementing compliant, practical transfer pricing policies and processes. The role will focus on transactions between Stripe’s legal entities that have characteristics commonly associated with the financial services sector, including intercompany arrangements supporting Stripe’s stablecoin-related activities.
This individual will work closely with teams across the organization and must be an excellent communicator who can explain complex transfer pricing concepts clearly to non-tax audiences. The ideal candidate will have transfer pricing experience in payments, fintech, banking, or another regulated financial services environment, as well as a track record of partnering effectively with cross-functional teams and other members of the tax organization.
Responsibilities
Partner with teams within and outside of Finance to develop, execute, and maintain transfer pricing policies for Stripe’s current and future operating structure and product offerings with a strong moral compass and integrity
Analyze financial information to design, prepare, and review detailed calculations, assist in preparing legal entity forecasts, and support the tax provision process
Address the transfer pricing impacts of special projects related to restructurings, acquisitions, and corporate initiatives, and ensure operating models are fit for purpose in the context of evolving global tax and transfer pricing frameworks and other regulations that apply to transactions between affiliates
Build relationships with product and business leaders to understand their organizational structure and activities, and adapt transfer pricing policies in response to changes
Assist finance, legal, and tax teams in government and regulatory audits, and support Stripe’s participation in tax audits, advance pricing agreements, and competent authority proceedings
Prepare and maintain transfer pricing documentation and compliance in accordance with Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) guidelines and local tax and regulatory requirements, ensuring efficiency and quality across a subset of assigned jurisdictions
Build or simplify transfer pricing models for clarity, efficiency, and ease of use
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
A bachelor’s degree or higher in accounting, economics, business, law, or a related field, and 10+ years of relevant experience
Strong knowledge of global transfer pricing laws and regulations, experience with international tax planning for a multinational, and experience in financial services, banking, fintech, payments, or another regulated industry
Experience managing transfer pricing documentation and compliance; practical experience with transfer pricing dispute resolution, including audits, advance pricing agreement negotiations, and competent authority negotiations; and experience developing, maintaining, and implementing intercompany agreements
Knowledge of financial accounting concepts, including accounting for intercompany transactions; professional experience with Excel, Oracle, and Smart View; and enjoyment of working with and digging into data from multiple sources
Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills, strong interpersonal and team-building capabilities across different functional areas and cultures, and curiosity, empathy, and humility
Preferred qualifications
An advanced degree or professional qualification in tax, accounting, economics, or law, such as a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) credential, Juris Doctor (JD), or Master of Laws (LLM)
Experience working in a high-growth, rapidly scaling environment
Working knowledge of Regulation W, Sections 23A and 23B of the Federal Reserve Act, or comparable affiliate transaction requirements, including pricing, documentation, governance, or monitoring considerations, with a practical understanding of how regulatory requirements affect operating models and affiliate arrangements
Experience with stablecoins, digital assets, wallets, on-chain financial infrastructure, payments, or treasury products
